Gaṇeśa’s divine vehicle takes Ballāla heavenward. Viśvāmitra confirms prediction occurred: she was born Kamalā, he a kṣatriya. Printed final45 versus total46 is retained as numbering uncertainty.
outcome: Future relief conditions and completed rebirth identified; Ballāla ascends.

cause: Daily prescribed worship continues.
details: Bhīma asks Dakṣa’s practice. At ruined forest Gaṇeśa shrine near Kauṇḍinya he practices Mudgala’s one-syllable mantra, worships and offers roots/fruit with imagined dakṣiṇā. Text says twelve years6, then21days8 before dawn dream: elephant garlands him, lifts him to shoulder and enters flagged city. Kamalā interprets elephant as Vināyaka and mount as kingship. Dakṣa promises her vehicle/villages/jewels and charitable rites if fulfilled; she wishes long life and steady reverence. Duration phrasing is preserved, not harmonized.
outcome: Dream predicts kingship; mother interprets and receives conditional promises.

cause: Royal death threatens succession.
details: At Kauṇḍinya King Candrasena dies through ripened karma and merits heaven by divine vehicle. Citizens and childless wife Sulabhā mourn, collapse and reproach separation. Ministers Sumantu and Manorañjana ask who will govern and propose following him. These ancient ministers are context-distinct from current Bhīma’s same-named ministers.
outcome: Court mourns with no heir.

cause: Funeral and continued vacancy require decision.
details: A learned Brahmin rebukes self-serving grief and orders funeral care by an adopted or other son; Sumantu performs rites, all give sesame water, then baths and household return follow. After13days they feed and honour queen. In succession uncertainty Mudgala arrives and prescribes royal elephant Gahana carrying lotus garland: whoever it garlands in assembly shall rule. All approve the sage’s supernormal insight.
outcome: Elephant-selection rule accepted.

cause: Mudgala’s selection rule enacted.
details: At auspicious assembly queen gives garland to decorated Gahana. It passes city candidates, leaves town and garlands Dakṣa worshipping Gaṇeśa, fulfilling dream. People honour king with clothes/jewels; heavenly flowers and music celebrate. Dakṣa gives gifts, honours mother, places her in palanquin, rides elephant and enters decorated city with two mounted ministers.
outcome: Dakṣa chosen king and brings mother to capital.

cause: Kingship prompts gratitude and further blessing.
details: Dakṣa sends Sumantu with vehicle/royal insignia to invite Mudgala, meets him, bows and seats sage on his throne. Attributing health and kingship to sage and identifying him devotionally with Vināyaka, king asks hand on his head to enjoy all wishes long. Mudgala assures no enemy-caused fear and fulfilment of every desired wish. King rewards sage/Brahmins/ministers and enlarges old Gaṇeśa temple at Kuṇḍina.
outcome: Protective blessing and temple enlargement follow.

details: Vallabha arrives on hearing news. King Vīrasena, instructed by Gaṇeśa in dream, gives his marriage-seeking daughter to Dakṣa. Their son is Bṛhadbhānu; successive line is Khaḍgadhara→Sulabha→Padmākara→Vapurdīpta→Citraseṇa→current Bhīma. Hearing ancestral line, Bhīma asks Viśvāmitra when/how Vināyaka will favour him. Exact ancestor counting against19.40 remains a collation task.
outcome: Marriage and descendant genealogy close ancestral Dakṣa sequence; present Bhīma resumes.

cause: Family exemplum establishes restored worship.
details: Vyāsa asks Bhīma’s remedy. Viśvāmitra teaches one-syllable mantra and directs observance in Dakṣa’s temple, promising wishes, four aims and return home. Bhīma and Cāruhāsinī return honoured by citizens/ministers. King practices fasting, mantra and constant Gaṇeśa awareness in Dakṣa shrine; seeing god everywhere people think him possessed. Gaṇeśa takes his hand, calls him liberated and offers wish; king says he knows only divine feet. Deity promises virtuous golden-bodied son and commands deity/Brahmin worship. Shortly son is born and named Rukmāṅgada amid gifts.
outcome: Initiation and devotion yield promised son’s birth.

cause: Promised son grows and inherits worship.
details: Bhīma entrusts growing Rukmāṅgada to Kapila for education; son grasps teaching on hearing and becomes learned/strong, compared with Gajakarṇa. Father consecrates him and gives priestly gifts; son increases Gaṇeśa devotion and recites father-taught one-syllable mantra daily. Hunting one day he kills game, becomes exhausted and reaches a sage’s peaceful hermitage.
outcome: Education, accession and hunt open new opponent episode.

cause: Hunt exhaustion leads to water request.
details: Exhausted Rukmāṅgada honours sage Vācaknavi and wife Mukundā. While sage bathes, prince addresses her as mother and requests cold water to live. Attracted, she demands affection; he refuses adultery through Vināyaka’s grace and rejects her water. She claims consensual relations exempt punishment and women had freedom in early ages, threatens destruction/exile, seizes and forcibly kisses him. He pushes her away and insists refusal; angry she curses him to leprosy and he leaves distressed.
outcome: Refusal of coercive sexual demand brings Mukundā’s curse.

cause: Curse manifests immediately after leaving.
details: Prince sees white diseased body replacing golden beauty, questions Gaṇeśa why a devotee suffers and recalls deity’s protective manifestations. Maintaining exclusive refuge, he refuses to show his appearance and resolves fasting unto death beneath banyan. Servants search unsuccessfully until night and go home.
outcome: Prince withdraws to fasting; servants cannot find him.

cause: Fasting prince encounters compassionate sage.
details: Rukmāṅgada sees Nārada in sky, honours and asks refuge, recounting hunt, water request, Mukundā’s unwanted kiss/demand, refusal and leprosy, and fears Bhīma’s grief. Nārada says he witnessed an old leprous Śūdra pilgrim at Vidarbha’s Kadamba city bathe in Gaṇeśakuṇḍa before Cintāmaṇi image, gain divine body and ascend by Gaṇeśa attendants’ vehicle to a non-returning abode. He prescribes bath, deity worship and Brahmin giving; prince is joyful.
outcome: Witnessed healing supplies remedy.

cause: Remedy motivates inquiry into site origin.
details: Before sage departs prince asks who installed image and first attained success, praising wandering sages’ aid. Nārada accepts question and promises complete account.
outcome: Nested Indra–Ahalyā episode opens.

cause: Indra requests a wondrous report.
details: Nārada says Indra honoured him in Amarāvatī and requested wonder. He described Gautama’s hermitage and Ahalyā’s beauty, claiming his own distraction; comparisons name Sāvitrī, Śacī, Lakṣmī, Girijā, Urvaśī, Menakā, Rambhā, Tilottamā, Anasūyā, Arundhatī, Sun’s wives Chāyā/Saṃjñā and Kaśyapa’s Aditi. He then vanished; this is Nārada’s narrated prior speech.
outcome: Beauty report excites Indra’s desire.

cause: Indra impersonates absent husband.
details: Indra, inflamed by Nārada’s report, assumes Gautama’s form and enters hermitage during sage’s bath. Ahalyā questions early return and daytime desire; impersonator invents seeing a bathing apsaras, threatens death, curse or renunciation unless served. Believing voice, appearance and manner are her husband, she follows his command and intercourse occurs.
outcome: Ahalyā is deceived by assumed form and fabricated explanation.

cause: Fragrance exposes impersonation.
details: Divine fragrance alarms Ahalyā; fearing scandal and husband’s response she demands stranger identify himself or face curse. Indra reveals ornaments/crown and identity as Śacī’s husband, then asks continued intimacy. Angry she accuses him of breaking chastity by deceit and anticipates Gautama’s curse. Number labels26/30 appear as56/32; sequence and final total32 retained without renumbered quotation.
outcome: Victim confronts revealed deceiver.

cause: Confession precedes angry judgment.
details: Gautama returns and asks why wife neither greets nor serves as usual. Trembling Ahalyā prostrates and explains mistaken obedience to his assumed form, fragrance-triggered suspicion and revelation under threat, then asks forgiveness. Sage, furious, accuses her of failing recognition and curses her to stone; he adds that Daśarathi Rāma’s foot-touch during forest wandering will restore her form. She immediately becomes stone; restoration remains future here.
outcome: Stone transformation realized; foot-touch relief promised.

cause: Offender seeks concealment.
details: Indra hears curse, considers hiding underwater and takes cat form. Gautama identifies him in meditation and says he will not burn deity to ashes but curses him, as Śacī’s husband, to a thousand bhagas. Transformation occurs immediately. Indra regrets disregarded elders, blaming Nārada’s words and desire, vows karmic expiation as animal and hides in lotus bud as indragopaka insect.
outcome: Thousand-mark curse manifests and offender hides.

cause: Indra’s absence threatens cosmic protection.
details: Nārada tells assembled gods led by Bṛhaspati of both curses. Concerned for Indra, Śacī and cosmic government, they seek Gautama together and praise sage-power, recounting Gautama’s same-day grain aid, Vālakhilya-created second Indra later made bird ruler at Brahmā’s plea, unnamed sage’s ocean-drinking, Gādhi’s son creating another world and Cyavana stopping Indra’s arm. They beg compassion for surrendered gods.
outcome: Collective intercession begins.

cause: Gods ask collective pardon and restoration.
details: Gautama welcomes gods and asks their request. They ask pardon and Indra’s return to office, citing Śiva burning Kāma while sage spared offender’s life. Gautama says unrepentant fallen deceiver lacks expiation but honours their collective plea: transmit Vināyaka’s six-syllable mantra; initiation will give divine body, convert all bhagas to eyes and restore office. Gods worship, circumambulate, receive leave and go to Indra.
outcome: Conditional mantra remedy offered through intercessors.

cause: Gods persuade offender to accept public remedy.
details: Gods with Nārada call Indra from lotus, advise confessing rather than hiding fault, and offer Gautama’s remedy, recalling Brahmā’s emission after seeing a toe at Girijā–Śiva wedding and Śiva’s remedy. Indra emerges foul and wounded, bathes and sips ritually; Bṛhaspati teaches six-syllable Gaṇeśa mantra. Initiation immediately yields divine body and1,000eyes; gods rejoice, shower flowers and sages bless.
outcome: Mantra initiation realizes bodily conversion.

cause: Bodily recovery prompts deeper devotional resolve.
details: Indra thanks gods and sages, confesses wrongful act following Nārada and asks how they won Gautama’s favour. They explain intercession and command Amarāvatī return. He refuses to return without Gaṇeśa’s favour, sends helpers home and remains to practice, acknowledging their restoration of him.
outcome: Indra postpones return pending deity’s favour.

cause: Unfinished desire for divine favour sustains austerity.
details: Indra practices six-syllable mantra beneath kadamba, nose-tip gaze, restraint and air-only diet for1,000years; ant hills and bushes cover motionless body. Brilliant four-armed Gaṇeśa appears and frightened practitioner mistakes him for obstacle. God reassures and identifies himself as meditated transcendent creator, pleased with austerity and ready to grant; Indra recognises and bows.
outcome: Deity appears and offers boon after1,000years.

cause: Restored devotee reflects on earlier neglected initiation.
details: Indra praises unknowable Gaṇeśa and recalls impermanent office earned by100sacrifices. He says Brahmā earlier taught this mantra and warned forgetting it would cause loss of office and distress; forgetting preceded Ahalyā’s violation. Bṛhaspati’s renewed instruction now produced1,000eyes and sight of deity.
outcome: Earlier warning and repeated initiation explicitly distinguished.

cause: God offers personal boon after austerity.
details: Indra asks constant nonforgetfulness and feet-directed mind, renaming Kadamba as Cintāmaṇipura, lake as Cintāmaṇitīrtha and bath/giving benefits of four aims and siddhis. Gaṇeśa affirms all requests and adds stable office, constant remembrance and divine appearance to accomplish tasks whenever crisis brings remembrance; site bath and thought-fulfilment promises are reiterated.
outcome: Devotion, site efficacy and protected office granted.

cause: Granted site efficacy receives installation.
details: Indra brings heavenly Gaṅgā for deity’s ablution and worship; after divine disappearance he installs crystal image and vast jewelled temple, bows/circumambulates and returns to office. Gaṅgā is said to continue daily ablution by his command. Nārada ends site history and instructs Rukmāṅgada to bathe for all-fault freedom, blesses him and departs.
outcome: Indra returns; narrator hands remedy back to prince.

cause: Site history provides remedy.
details: Vyāsa asks prince’s next step. Army finds diseased Rukmāṅgada after searching mountains/woods/rivers; he recounts curse and Nārada’s prescription, invites them to bathe, give and worship then return. At sight of Gaṇeśatīrtha he already gains former golden divine body, before the subsequently narrated bath; he recognises Nārada’s true instruction.
outcome: Arrival and sight heal before ritual bath.

cause: Healed prince completes worship and giving.
details: After bath, Brahmin gifts and Vināyaka worship, prince and witnesses see radiant aerial vehicle with Gaṇeśa attendants, apsarases and kinnaras. He asks identity; messengers explain deity’s command to bring surrendered devotee Rukmāṅgada to himself after fulfilled pilgrimage. Prince marvels at favour and honours them, comparing his limited mind with transcendent divine cause.
outcome: Divine invitation to ascent offered.

cause: Devotee requests inclusion of parents.
details: Prince refuses ascent without father Bhīma and mother Cāruhāsinī, noting her devotion. Messengers prescribe bathing for them and transfer merit, then they too can ascend. Prince makes kuśa proxies, recites symbolic bath mantra and bathes for all village people. He returns by vehicle to Kauṇḍinya with retinue, transfers merit to parents and all inhabitants; additional vehicles arrive and everyone, down to children and outcastes, ascends to Vināyaka. Devoted hearing of this greatness is promised same destination.
outcome: Proxy merit transfer allows collective ascent and closes prince’s pilgrimage arc.

details: Nested narrators shift from Upāsanā to Krīḍā, answering requests for manifestations, opponents and childhood exploits; Viṣṇu gives the four-age manifestation synopsis.
Śāradā bears twins after nine months; Rudraketu performs birth, ancestral and naming rites, distributes gifts and feeds the community. Astrologers name Devāntaka and Narāntaka.

Exceptional growth attracts Nārada. Parents request long life, power, fame, knowledge and enemy punishment. Nārada gives five-syllable Śiva instruction and protective blessing; twins seek permission to practice.

Twins undertake forest austerity on one big toe, Śiva meditation and mantra. Air-only and leaf-only phases are reported; total is10000years although specified phases total4000. Their tapas dims the Sun and pacifies beasts.
Śiva appears with Umā. Twins praise him and request broad death exclusions, three-world rule and devotion. Śiva grants all requested benefits and touches their heads.
Twins return, report boon and receive parental welcome, food and brāhmaṇa blessings.
After morning ritual and gifts, elder undertakes heaven conquest and younger earth/Pātāla.
Devāntaka ravages Amarāvatī, terrifies guards and demands offices under threat. Indra mounts elephant, rallies gods and attacks with vajra.
Vajra shatters without hurting Devāntaka; fist defeats Indra. Devāntaka pursues fleeing Indra but refuses a rear attack, calling for face combat.

Gods lose stations and shelter in a golden cave. Consecrated Devāntaka takes Amarāvatī, Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha and assigns demon officials. Brahmā retreats with gods; Viṣṇu/Lakṣmī retreat to Milk Ocean.

Narāntaka conquers earth through killing and submission: retains loyal vassals, installs dead kings’ sons as tributaries and replaces resisters with demons. Sages suspend visible rites/tapas but mentally retain Vedic recitation.
Demons assume Garuḍa forms and devour Nāgas. Śeṣa negotiates tribute with gifts; despite agreement an overseer/army stays in Rasātala, with rebellion reporting and threatened destruction.
Brothers exchange reports and scarce gifts across their realms. Somakānta asks Bhṛgu how and by what form/weapons they died; the nested Brahmā–Vyāsa narrative promises that continuation.
Aditi asks supreme Lord as son to serve him; Kaśyapa instructs name mantra, meditation, nyāsa and observance, authorizes forest tapas.
Air-only austerity and concentrated practice lead to ten-armed divine appearance. Aditi faints from radiance, is reassured, and asks gentle form and sonship for devotion and worldly protection.
Vināyaka grants promised sonship, protection, wicked destruction and fulfillment of wishes, disappears. Aditi reports to Kaśyapa; both rejoice.

Earth petitions against demonic burden and threatens sinking. Brahmā and displaced gods/sages jointly praise Vināyaka; sky voice announces Kaśyapa-home incarnation, offices restored and demon destruction; Earth reassured.
After nine months Aditi bears divine ten-armed child. He recalls prior meditation/grant and promises parent service, earth burden removal, gods’ restoration and destruction of demons.
Parents request ordinary child appearance and freedom to manifest needed forms. Divine form withdrawn; two-armed crying child brings fertility/vegetation effects, gods’ joy and demons’ fear.
Birth rites, nursing, purification and community gifts follow. Father names child Mahotkaṭa on eleventh day; child rapidly grows.
Sages visit after Nārada’s report, receive hospitality, recognize incarnation/32signs, predict obstacles removed and urge constant care; worship and petition protection.
Virajā swallows unattended infant, flies/drinks/collapses. Child grows inside, tears belly and stands on chest. Demoness dies and through divine contact attains his abode, freed from return.
Aditi searches/laments missing son, finds him on corpse, embraces and returns. Kaśyapa links survival to sages’ words, performs protective/peace rites and gifts, mandates never leave child.
Demons arrive as parrots after Virajā’s death. Child catches them, survives beak/wing blows and slams both dead. Giant bodies burned; peace rites and parental guarding admonition follow.
Fourth-year child joins mother’s sacred bath and enters water. Crocodile seizes him; rescue fails. After feigned helplessness he throws crocodile ashore, revealing divine Gandharva.
Gandharva recalls wedding neglect of Bhṛgu, crocodile curse and conditional release by Gajānana/Kaśyapa son’s touch. Recognizes fulfillment, praises/worships child and departs.
Aditi nurses, returns and reports. Kaśyapa identifies supreme Lord playfully human, predicts further divine exploits and urges devotion.
Three Viṣṇu-devoted musicians pause en route Kailāsa, are honored and persuaded to stay for meal. Bath and five-deity worship precede meditation.
Child removes five images and hides in fire room. Guests refuse meal without images. Father follows disciples’ hint, threatens child with stick; child denies and cries.

Mother’s mouth inspection reveals cosmos and she faints; father/guests see14worlds/deities. Father recognizes Lord and bows. Guests then behold child as five deities and cosmic forms, worship and eat offered food.

Three praise transcendence, knowledge/renunciation/devotion and warn siddhi attachment causes fall. Ask continuous remembrance/devotion in all births and liberation by grace. No spoken grant; depart for Kailāsa.

Fifth-year tonsure/initiation attacked by five disguised brāhmaṇa demons. Injured child consecrates/throws five rice grains, kills all. Rites complete with sacred equipment, Sāvitrī, alms, instruction and gifts; Vasiṣṭha brings child to Brahmā.
Assembly gives lotus, ornaments, weapons, mount, seat, fire/strength and names. Rāma’s mother urges demons destroyed. Indra alone refuses gift/worship due pride; Kaśyapa counsels honoring deeds.
Kaśyapa cites earlier exploits; Indra demands own proof and orders wind then fire attack. Cosmic wind cannot move child or hair; child swallows destructive fire.
Cosmic form with universes in hairs appears. Indra enters one and wanders12years unable exit, surrenders and requests ordinary form. Instantly back in assembly, bows publicly.

Indra praises, gifts goad/wish tree/two serving women and names Vināyaka. Lord grants battlefield fearlessness, prescribes thrice-daily hymn and devotional recitation benefits. Gods rejoice and disperse.
Taunting Sindūra rejects offered bowed submission. Lord shows cosmic form; sword attack answered by throat grip and hand crushing, then blood anointing and names.
Gods/sages/kings celebrate restored order, worship, establish temple and name Sindūraha; sight/remembrance benefits declared.
Vareṇya recognizes son, repents abandonment. Lord embraces him, recalls prior joint1000divine-year sonship request/grant and fulfilled incarnation mission, announces departure.

Vareṇya asks liberation yoga. Lord seats/blesses/teaches/reveals cosmos. Narrator summarizes subsequent forest renunciation and identity realization; Vyāsa asks to hear teaching. Detailed instruction follows in138–148, not a second historical teaching.
Nested transmission introduces king’s yoga question and Lord’s reply.

Yoga definition excludes worldly/divine acquisitions; fivefold non-difference, cosmic self/Brahman, offered duty, equality and stable intellect/sense mastery taught. Desire→anger→memory/intellect ruin and knowledge liberation described.
King asks knowledge/action priority then cause of unwilling sin; Lord teaches unattached offered action, sacrificial reciprocity/world example, guṇa agency, own duty and conquest of desire/anger.

Lord recalls primordial teaching lineage and recurrent divine births. King challenges present birth versus past teaching; Lord explains recollection and māyā incarnation, then fruits, karma/nonaction, sacrifices, knowledge/guru/holy-company and faith.

King asks renunciation/action then true happiness; same liberating fruit, action yoga preferred, equanimity, inward bliss, breath-restraint measures and resulting three-time knowledge/world mastery taught.

Lord teaches proper circumstances/moderation, mind practice and dangers; king asks uncontrollable mind and fallen yogin fate. Guru grace/holy company/dispassion/practice and favorable rebirth explained.
Lower/higher prakṛti, cosmic immanence, māyā, rare knowledge and disposition fruits taught; death remembrance/no return, other deity worlds, divine yoga-kṣema and two routes announced.
King asks routes/Brahman/rebirth; Lord explains routes, worship forms/offerings, mental/desireless priority, all āśrama eligibility, no deity hatred, nyāsa/japa from guru and liberation/refuge.

King asks cosmic form after Nārada’s account; Lord creates knowledge sight. King describes cosmos/terrifying body, asks gentle form. Lord emphasizes grace/devotion over learning/rites alone, grants gentle vision instruction.

King asks embodied/unmanifest worship and field/knower. Lord gives devotion/alternative practice hierarchy, dear devotee qualities, psychophysical field and inner knower/Brahman, guṇa binding/results and worship-responsive forms.
Divine/asuric/rākṣasic character, consequences, devotion by guṇas and four destructive gates taught; these are ethical teaching categories, not named armies or enacted contemporary punishments.
Threefold austerity/gift/knowledge/action/actor/happiness classifications, Oṃ Tat Sat and varṇa duties taught; Lord finishes and directs secret practice.

Vareṇya follows, renounces kingdom/family, forest practice attains liberation. Narrator gives hearing/teaching/guru-understood recitation, pilgrimage/fourth-day and Bhādra clay-image/seven-recitation benefits.

Lord stays royal worshipped. Vyāsa questions differing birth/face/opponent accounts; Brahmā explains kalpa variation and divine freedom, compares other textual traditions and closes prior-age narrative.

Brahmā predicts late Kali decline and future horse/sword manifestation creating army/weapons, destroying oppressive hosts and restoring surviving brāhmaṇas/Kṛta dharma; future statements remain prospective.
Frame returns: Vyāsa thanks Brahmā, receives departure permission, performs sheltered forest one-syllable mantra tapas12years; Lord appears. Boon in150 remains next target.

Mudgala tells Dakṣa the campaign’s purpose. Matsara and demons approach Śukra, request consecration as their king and receive his agreement. Named chiefs assemble; Veda-knowing Brahmins consecrate Matsara with Ṛg/Yajus/Sāman formulas, Uśanas directing the rites. The assembly rejoices and returns home.
outcome: Matsara is consecrated demon king.

details: Matsara summons the Asuras to conquer the three worlds. Fourfold forces muster with arms, trees, rocks and mountains: infantry, decorated elephants, swift horsemen, chariots and other animal mounts. His decorated chariot has one hundred asses; both sons ride horses ahead, Virocana and other chiefs around him.
outcome: Army marches to conquest.

details: Demon forces defeat terrestrial rulers: some flee, some surrender, warriors die fighting. Sons of dead rulers are installed as tributaries; surrendered kings retain office. Demons govern rulerless regions and are stationed beside local kings. Matsara rejoices after conquering the islanded earth.
outcome: Earth is subordinated under tribute and surveillance.

details: Demons destroy Nāga gardens in Pātāla. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Kambala and Aśvatara lead resistance: arms and missiles first repel demons; returning chiefs repel Nāgas. Serpent poison-flames burn demons, weapons and mounts; Śukra’s vidyā removes poison. A Garuḍa missile produces bird assailants, burnt by Vāsuki’s poison-fire. Virocana and chiefs themselves become Garuḍas by māyā and overwhelm Nāgas.
outcome: Māyā transformations overcome the first failed bird missile.

details: Śeṣa comes conciliating, asks why fellow Pātāla residents wage war, and addresses demons as brothers. Virocana demands submission to Matsara’s universal authority or destruction. Śeṣa agrees, offers annual tribute and jewels, withdraws with Vāsuki and others. Victorious demons march against Varuṇa.
outcome: Pātāla settles through annual tribute.

details: Matsara sends Varuṇa an ultimatum: submit in office or be killed. Makara-mounted Varuṇa advances with noose and aquatic forces. Virocana, Mahiṣāsura, Śumbha and Andhaka fight them. After three days demons fall; Kāvya restores their awareness, battle resumes and Virocana captures Varuṇa. Kubera hears the news and flees to Śiva on Kailāsa; demons occupy Alakā and march with captive Varuṇa against Yama.
outcome: Varuṇa captured; Alakā occupied after Kubera’s flight.

details: Buffalo-mounted Yama advances with staff, Death, diseases and attendants. Five days of fighting defeat demons until Viṣayapriya fights Death and afflicts diseases. He disables Yama’s buffalo and fells Yama. Rising, Yama strikes him with Kāladanda; the staff instead falls to earth, and Viṣayapriya captures him. Demons praise the son’s feat.
outcome: Viṣayapriya captures Yama despite the Death-staff attack.

details: Demons proceed with captive Yama to Amarāvatī. Agni, Vāyu, Viśvedevas, Sādhyas, Rudras, Vasus, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, planets, moon, sun and Ādityas join Indra on Airāvata with vajra. Seven nights end in demon flight and fainting chiefs. Sundarapriya attacks the gods; Indra’s vajra does not move him. He disables Airāvata, seizes Indra by the foot and captures him. Other gods die, fall, flee or are captured; Matsara gains heaven.
outcome: Sundarapriya captures Indra; Matsara rules heaven.

details: Fleeing gods ask Kaśyapa to protect them and release Indra. With Vasiṣṭha, gods and sages, Kaśyapa petitions Brahmā to restore proper stations. Brahmā admits Matsara’s Śiva-boon makes him unconquerable and takes them to Viṣṇu, who also admits inability. They seek Śiva, who explains his own fierce-austerity grant and inability to destroy the demon. Viṣṇu chooses refuge at Kailāsa rather than submission, predicts Matsara will take Vaikuṇṭha and Satyaloka but spare Kailāsa out of devotion. Śiva remains anxious.
outcome: Gods cluster at Kailāsa; their expectation will be challenged.

details: Matsara occupies Indra’s throne, uses Airāvata, receives frightened celestial entertainers and redistributes divine offices to demon chiefs. He resents Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Rudra not paying homage. Andhaka is sent to summon them under threat, finds Satyaloka and Vaikuṇṭha empty, then enters Kailāsa and receives a seat. He delivers the demand. Śiva asserts that Matsara wins through his boon and threatens to burn him; he releases Andhaka because he is an envoy and orders him to report.
outcome: Andhaka returns with Śiva’s refusal.

details: Andhaka praises Kailāsa’s unmatched splendour. Chiefs urge attack; Matsara credits his own austerity and karma, rejecting Śiva’s boast as giver. He argues desire-driven action yields gains and Brahman-dedicated action liberation, and claims world creation, preservation and destruction depend on karma rather than the three gods. Demons march to Kailāsa, wound Śiva’s guards, who flee and report.
outcome: Matsara attacks his former boon-grantor’s domain.

details: Śiva arms with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Kāma, Vasus, Kubera, moon, sun, Agni, Vāyu, Kālāgni Rudra, Bhairavas, Vīrabhadra, Nandin, Bhṛṅgin, Puṣpadanta, Mahākāla, Mahākālī and Kārttikeya. Bull-mounted Śiva advances. Confused armies counter weapons and wrestle; chiefs enter named duels while Matsara watches. Seven days/nights end with gods overpowering and felling the demon chiefs and sons.
outcome: Gods gain a temporary victory.

details: Matsara enters roaring and showers arrows: Senānī, Agni, Nandin, Vīrabhadra, sun, moon, Vāyu, Kālāgni Rudra, Mahākālī, Bhṛṅgin’s Gaṇas, Kubera and Brahmā fall. He counters Viṣṇu’s thousand-arrow shower and fells him with a hundred. Śiva’s trident is ineffective and falls; Matsara nooses his neck and draws him like a bound animal. He taunts Śiva that both owe capacity to karma, captures other gods and enjoys Kailāsa.
outcome: Śiva and divine defenders are captured.

details: Matsara assigns Kailāsa to Sundarapriya, Vaikuṇṭha to the son here written Vijayapriya, Satyaloka to Prahlāda, and Indra’s region to Virocana. He creates Matsarāvāsaka on earth. He releases Śiva and gods with permission to go wherever they wish provided they obey his orders. They shelter anxiously in mountain valleys and caves.
outcome: Divine captives are released under Matsara’s command.

details: Matsara orders gods’ images broken and cast into water, and installs his images in regions, settlements and houses. He coerces Brahmins to perform sacrifice, Gāyatrī and Agnihotra in his name and promises wealth and heaven; feeding demons pleases him. Some sages keep rites in wild forests, while others abandon duties from fear. Sacrificial exclamations cease; gods suffer starvation and cannot devise his destruction.
outcome: Suppressed worship produces divine deprivation.

details: Wandering Dattātreya arrives, a fearless naked yogin and Gaṇarāja devotee. Gods honor him, massage his feet and offer fruit. Śiva asks a destruction strategy, describing displacement and starvation. Dattātreya says Śiva’s own claim to unique lordship is Matsara in his heart; conquer envy through yoga and Gaṇeśa worship. He recounts his own one-syllable worship and non-separation from Gaṇeśa, prescribes that worship, tells Śiva first to destroy inner Matsara then the demon, and leaves.
outcome: Dattātreya prescribes inner reform and one-syllable worship.

details: Śiva repeats Dattātreya’s counsel; gods and sages worship Gaṇeśa with the one-syllable mantra for a thousand divine years. They use diverse seats, fasting or leaves/air/water, breath control, toe-standing, mental worship, flowers and circumambulation. Vakratunda appears as radiant Brahman, lion-mounted, elephant-faced, four-armed with noose/goad and boon/fearlessness gestures, Siddhi left and Buddhi right. The alarmed petitioners ask gentleness; he identifies himself and softens his radiance. They worship with sixteen services and begin a hymn.
outcome: Vakratunda manifests and accepts worship.

details: Gods and sages hymn Vakratunda’s forms and yoga unity, ask lasting devotion and destruction of Matsara for the afflicted world. Vakratunda promises the hymn will confer siddhis and desired objects and that he will remove Matsara. He explains that gods, humans, Nāgas and the world belong to the five-element/three-guṇa/eight-envelope domain from which Matsara has no fear, making destruction difficult, yet promises their welfare.
outcome: Vakratunda accepts the rescue request and states its difficulty.

details: Vakratunda remembers his army; Pramoda, Āmodaka and elephant-faced, four-armed Gaṇas manifest, variously lion-, mouse-, peacock-, Śeṣa- or horse-mounted. They offer obedience and say one could destroy Matsara. Vakratunda explains that he created the demon through māyā for play: immediate annihilation would end the play. He orders battle in his presence and says a form without the eight envelopes can kill him instantly. Gods and sages rejoice; the whole host goes to the city named Īrṣyā.
outcome: Vakratunda deliberately permits the campaign instead of immediate annihilation.

details: Matsara enjoys celestial company and all mentally wished objects through austerity and boon. A sky-voice announces Vakratunda’s arrival to kill him; he faints. Demons search the sky unsuccessfully and restore him. He invokes immunity against eight-envelope beings. Prahlāda and chiefs argue the defeated gods may have produced an illusion, dismiss the voice, and obtain permission to find and kill them.
outcome: The warning triggers a demon reconnaissance rather than surrender.

details: Searching chiefs see elephant-human Vakratunda praised by gods, fear the warning is true and return to report rather than risk dying before reporting. Vakratunda is encamped five yojanas from Īrṣyāpura. Matsara first pales, then orders his army to attack. Frightened gods petition immediate protection; lion-mounted Vakratunda with noose/goad promises rescue and roars, terrifying all worlds and demons. Chiefs offer to fight while Matsara watches.
outcome: Matsara’s fourfold host advances; chiefs begin battle.

details: Prahlāda-led demons rain weapons; Viṣṇu-led gods respond. Countered missiles, swords, maces, nooses and wrestling generate casualties and dust that hides friend from foe. Blood settles the dust; matching fourfold units fight one another. Wounded troops and alternating advances/falls continue without night rest for five days, with neither side prevailing.
outcome: Five-day stalemate opens the chief-led reversals.

details: Prahlāda’s Anala missile burns gods and mounts; Indra prepares Megha missile, but Prahlāda cuts his bow before release. Indra’s vajra fells Prahlāda; Mahiṣa maces Indra unconscious. Agni flames Mahiṣa, who becomes water and floods him, cuts Agni’s śakti and becomes a buffalo to fell him with horns. Yama staffs Mahiṣa down; Virocana swords Yama down. Varuṇa nooses Virocana, but Andhaka cuts the noose and maces Varuṇa. Vāyu swords Andhaka down; Śambara clubs Vāyu down. Virocana’s arrows fell Kubera.
outcome: Successive interventions reverse both sides’ advantages.

details: Viṣṇu’s mace splits Virocana’s chest leaving him dead-like; discus fells Andhaka, arrows fell Śambara, and discus/mace kill or disable demons. Prahlāda recovers, wounds gods, fights Viṣṇu with mace and fells Garuḍa with sword. As Viṣṇu’s discus approaches, Prahlāda remembers Janārdana and releases a Nārāyaṇa missile. It repels the discus, burns gods, hits Keśava’s heart and leaves him unconscious, dead-like.
outcome: Nārāyaṇa missile defeats the discus and disables Viṣṇu.

details: Seeing gods and sages burnt, Śiva uses Pināka to release Pāśupata. It fights Nārāyaṇa missile in the sky; the gods rejoice. Śiva then throws trident, kills many demons, strikes Prahlāda’s heart and fells him. Other chiefs die or faint; Matsara’s two sons Sundarapriya and Viṣayapriya approach Śiva angrily.
outcome: Śiva temporarily defeats the chiefs; sons enter.

details: Dakṣa asks for more detail; Mudgala answers that even great gods cannot recount all Vakratunda’s power. The sons challenge Śiva, promising to kill him, Vakratunda, gods and sages. Śiva answers that Vakratunda came to reduce earth’s burden, reversed their former time through changed karma, and will enable him to destroy them. Sons counter his arrows; their Pāśupata missile nullifies his trident, hits his heart and fells Śiva unconscious.
outcome: Even the newly confident Śiva falls to the sons’ missile.

details: Vakratunda sends eight chief Gaṇas with their troops: Pramoda, Āmoda, Brahmapriya, Yogapriya, Svānandabhoktṛ, Jñānamaya, Sarvaga and Sarvavit. Their look restores gods from fainting, fatigue and wounds, with doubled energy. Kavi restores demon forces to life and health. Gaṇas’ weapons sever demons; Brahmapriya seizes Śukra and throws him in a distant cave. Demons resolve to die fighting or rescue their guru, disable gods again, but the armed Gaṇas fell the chiefs and kill or disable the army.
outcome: Śukra’s capture removes the rescuing guru from the active battle.

details: Both sons challenge Pramoda’s Gaṇas and rain arrows. Sarvaga and Sarvavit counter the arrows and destroy demon troops. When the frightened sons prepare Agni missiles, two axes arrive before release and sever their heads. Survivors report both sons certainly dead, while they cannot tell if Prahlāda and others are dead or dead-like; they urge Matsara to abandon pride and surrender to protect the remaining demons.
outcome: Both sons die; survivors counsel surrender.

details: News of his sons’ death makes Matsara faint; restored after two muhūrtas, he laments lost children, supposedly failed immortality/fearlessness boon, and fate’s victory over effort. Elders comfort him: bodies die, self does not; relatives must perform funerary rites. They urge ritual duty, attack or surrender, and avoiding giving enemies joy by grief. Matsara instead takes the surviving army to battle.
outcome: Matsara chooses battle after consolation and alternative counsel.

details: Gods warn Vakratunda about Matsara’s sovereignty, timely rain, fruit, suppressed disease/theft, monopolized worship and sacrifices, displaced gods and disabled sages, seized women and immunity from eight-envelope beings. Vakratunda reassures them and advances lion-mounted with one tusk, noose and goad. Matsara threatens a one-arrow victory, invokes claimed earth-splitting and mountain-crushing strength, and offers Vakratunda life under his command in the forest while threatening the instigating gods and sages.
outcome: Final confrontation begins with threats and invocation of immunity.

details: Vakratunda says he is neither god, human, Asura, Nāga, Gandharva nor mountain, nor a creature from varied birth-origins or the eight envelopes, but joy-giving Brahman. He came to restore gods and sages; Matsara’s boon-merit has loosened through accumulated sin. He offers survival if Matsara surrenders and abandons hatred of dharma and gods. Astonished, Matsara respectfully asks how attribute-free Brahman can have form and favor gods over demons.
outcome: Matsara moves from threats to a doctrinal question, without a physical final duel.

details: Vakratunda explains creation as play with each being’s own dharma, his indwelling control through Puruṣa and Prakṛti, and conditional impartiality. When gods abandon duty to uproot demons or obstruct austerity, he inspires and grants demons boons against them. When demons abandon duty to uproot gods, he reveals their vulnerable means through the gods or takes form against demons the gods cannot conquer. He remains Brahman in both when they follow duty. Matsara oppressed gods through abandoning his own dharma, so he came against him.
outcome: The apparent favoritism is explained as restoring disrupted dharma.

details: Vakratunda shows his Brahman form in a point; by the grace and fruit of that vision Matsara receives divine sight. He sees the form beyond body/embodied, guṇas and māyā, with attributed body, attribute-free elephant head and their yoga unity. He bows, hymns the deity’s Brahman/yogic form, four arms, lion mount, Siddhi and Buddhi lordship, and seeks refuge and passage beyond worldly existence. He repeatedly falls at the feet and stands with folded hands.
outcome: Divine sight leads to praise and surrender.

details: Vakratunda declines to destroy a surrendered devotee, offers a boon, and promises Matsara’s hymn sovereignty, health, wealth, family and four aims. Matsara requests firm devotion, affection for Vakratunda’s devotees, and a place/livelihood with welfare. Vakratunda grants unwavering devotion and directs him to protect beings following their dharma and devotees. He must cause no obstruction wherever the deity’s image is worshipped or remembered at beginnings. Elsewhere he may act as an Asura, take fruits from karma/knowledge actors and rule in their hearts; toward devotion he must act as servant. Matsara accepts joyfully.
outcome: Matsara survives under restricted protective/obstructive duties.

details: Seeing Matsara at peace, gods and sages rejoice and hymn Vakratunda as Brahman encompassing and transcending forms, cosmic elements, deities, senses, creation/preservation/destruction, karma fruits, family and natural forms. They praise the demon’s transformation to peace and world’s joy, admit the deity exceeds Vedas, scriptures and yoga comprehension, and stand silent with folded hands. Vakratunda welcomes the praise.
outcome: Peace prompts final hymn and boon offer.

details: Vakratunda promises the hymn desired enjoyments, descendants, enjoyment/liberation, siddhis and insight. A thousand repetitions free a prisoner; recitation forgives offences, and twenty-one repetitions on twenty-one days grant what is contemplated. The praising gods/sages will be free of obstruction and devoted to their own dharma. Offered a boon, they request unwavering devotion as sufficient for all siddhis; he grants it.
outcome: Gods and sages receive unwavering devotion.

details: Vakratunda vanishes before gods and sages and dwells in Svānanda. Saddened gods and sages return to their own stations contemplating him. Matsara returns to his station with demons, abiding peacefully; demons then return to their separate homes. Mudgala explains Vakratunda creates, preserves and destroys and through incarnations restores gods, demons and humans to their respective duties.
outcome: Divine offices and ordinary homes are restored; Matsara lives peacefully.

details: Mudgala says Vakratunda’s incarnations are innumerable, beyond exhaustive narration by great gods, sages or Vedas. He mentions Dhundhirāja becoming Śiva’s son for Divodāsa’s pacification, manifestation before Vāmana to grant a boon, and Brahmā’s obstructed creation after failing to remember Vakratunda: Matsara entered him; refuge in the deity removed the obstacle. These are explicit brief previews, not fully extracted arcs.
outcome: Chapter39 closes the campaign and previews distinct stories.

details: Dakṣa asks how Brahmā worshipped Vakratunda. Mudgala recalls Gaṇeśa creating five divine lords and empowering them through austerity/boon. Beginning creation without remembering or worshipping Gaṇeśa, Brahmā prides himself on indispensability: without his creation, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Śakti and sun lack their functions. Many-eyed/many-faced Vighna hosts batter and toy with him. He relinquishes pride, takes refuge, remembers and hymns Gaṇeśa; the hosts vanish.
outcome: Humiliation and recollection remove the immediate obstruction.

details: Freed of obstacles, Brahmā propitiates Vakratunda with six-syllable mantra, feeding on air, standing on toe-tip, holding unwavering mental focus. After a divine thousand of austerity, disturbing beings, Vakratunda comes lion-mounted, three-eyed, elephant-faced, four-armed, with noose/goad/boon/fearlessness, Siddhi/Buddhi, Cintāmaṇi, Śeṣa at navel and red body. Brahmā fears the radiance and requests gentleness. Vakratunda softens it, explains the form ordinarily belongs to Svānanda and manifested through Brahmā’s devotion, then offers wishes.
outcome: Gentle manifestation prompts Brahmā’s hymn and boon request.

details: Brahmā praises Vakratunda’s Brahman, lion/elephant/four-arm form and Siddhi/Buddhi, requests unwavering devotion, unobstructed creative capacity, and the deity dwelling at home as son through māyā, freeing parental bondage and allowing continuous nurture/worship. Vakratunda grants all: creative power, obstacles removed by remembrance, desired objects, and rescuing sonhood through māyā/aṃśa; hymn grants all and Brahmanhood. He vanishes; Brahmā creates the whole animate/inanimate three worlds properly and rests remembering Vakratunda.
outcome: Creation restored; meditation-son promise awaits fulfilment.

details: Wind shakes Brahmā and Dambha manifests from his body-tremor as a great four-armed armed man. Asked identity, he claims birth from Brahmā’s tremor and sonhood, requests name, place and livelihood. Brahmā laughingly names him Dambha because of his boast, permits movement everywhere and enjoyments. Dambha bows and circles him, reaches earth, resents perceived disrespect and vows to remove Brahmā’s pride. He seeks Kavi, receives a mantra, and worships Brahmā foodless on one foot for ten thousand years, disturbing creation. Pleased Brahmā arrives with gods, astonished at his wooden-stillness and offers a boon.
outcome: Dambha’s retaliation motive leads to intense worship of his origin deity.

details: Offered wishes, Dambha hymns Brahmā as threefold Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva and all creation. He asks three-world rule, no death from five-element beings, no equal in battle, undivided sovereignty with health. Brahmā grants all requested and any contemplated object’s success, then disappears. Dambha establishes beautiful Śobhana city on earth. Śukra summons demons, comes with Brahman-knowing sages and has Brahmins consecrate him at auspicious time. The festival ends with chiefs remaining in the city.
outcome: Brahmā’s grant supports Dambha’s demon kingship.

details: Suhuṇḍa, Huṇḍa, Rukmaketu, Madyapa, Sakopa, Krodhāsura, Kāmāsura, Rāsabhāsura and other chiefs urge conquest as Dambha’s servants. He agrees, summons Śukra and accepts his counsel, then marches with fourfold forces, defeats terrestrial kings and Pātāla Nāgas, and goes to heaven. Indra’s vajra burns and crushes demons and makes them flee; Dambha’s discus fells Indra, arrows harm gods. Recovering Indra flees to live; Dambha sits on Airāvata and Indra’s throne.
outcome: Dambha conquers three worlds; Indra abandons his office.

details: Indra and gods take refuge in Brahmā, then Viṣṇu and Śiva. Śiva angrily challenges Dambha; forty days of destructive battle follow. Dambha’s arrows fell divine chiefs. Śiva’s trident fells Dambha, who rises immediately and hurls discus, felling Śiva for half a prahara. Regaining consciousness, Śiva flees with gods to the forest. Dambha installs demons in Satyaloka, Vaikuṇṭha, Kailāsa, Amarāvatī and other divine cities, then returns to Śobhana ruling three worlds.
outcome: Dambha supplants divine offices after reversible defeats on both sides.

details: Dambha orders karma destroyed. Demons bind and beat Brahmins, break sacrificial spaces and trees, destroy tīrthas and temples. Some Brahmins die or abandon duties, others flee forests; sacrificial exclamations and social dharma cease. Gods, dependent on ritual food, appeal to Brahmā as creator/provider and giver of fearlessness: without karma and food they face starvation and death.
outcome: Suppression of sacrifice provokes divine appeal for rescue.

details: Unable to devise rescue, Brahmā advises one-syllable worship of Vakratunda. Gods/sages worship; he meditates on the previously seen Siddhi/Buddhi-bearing form. After a hundred years he sees the speaking form in his heart, then it emerges with Siddhi and Buddhi. Vakratunda says he arose from Brahmā’s meditation, is dhyānaja, and fulfils the former requested sonhood. Brahmā bows and worships all three. The narrative calls him mental son, Siddhi/Buddhi daughters, and describes Vakratunda as with wife/wives (sabhāryaka) while all prepare a hymn.
outcome: Promised sonhood is fulfilled by meditation-origin, not womb birth.

details: Brahmā with gods/sages hymns the all-form Brahman deity and marvels that the meditated Siddhi/Buddhi-bearing Brahman came out as his son. Brahmā and Brahmins perform birth rites; on day eleven name him Siddhibuddhipati. He plays as a child, Sāvitrī nurses him, and his deeds please mother and father. At two years, with Siddhi/Buddhi, he asks why father dwells sorrowfully in forest. Brahmā tells Dambha’s story. The child promises to destroy Dambha and restore offices, goes lion-mounted with Siddhi/Buddhi near the city, and sends Indra to demand own-dharma, restored sacrificial food and social order. Dambha spares Indra as envoy, otherwise threatens imprisonment, and sets battle on fifth day. Indra reports and is praised.
outcome: A new child manifestation offers rescue and attempts conciliation.

details: Dambha summons Kavi/Śukra, prostrates, receives a gold seat and asks who Siddhi/Buddhi and their lord are. Śukra explains Siddhi as alluring māyā and people’s pursuit of worldly/otherworldly/Brahman fulfilment, left at Gaṇeśa’s side; Buddhi as knowledge/mind with five citta states and innumerable variants, at his right. Both māyās were formed from the deity’s own limb for play; Svānanda is Brahman and his abode. Brahmā requested sonhood to remove parental bondage; this deity came accordingly. He warns Dambha to surrender because this form will restore dharma and destroy him.
outcome: Guru explains the opponent’s identity, powers and manifestation purpose.

details: Dambha asks why impartial Gaṇeśa, from whom dharma/adharma arise, protects one and destroys the other. Kāvya explains an ordered world with separate places: greed-driven excess adharma strengthens Asuras and weakens gods, prompting Gaṇeśa to restore dharma; excessive dharma threatens demon root-destruction, so he grants demons boons to restore adharma’s assigned place. Neither party is self/other to him; greed-driven imbalance draws intervention. Dambha meditates privately, concludes that seeking siddhi or welfare while abandoning their lord causes failure, resolves surrender and sleeps fearlessly with Gaṇeśa in his heart.
outcome: Doctrinal answer changes Dambha’s decision before battle.

details: Next morning Dambha abandons Asura disposition and tells assembled demons before Śukra that guru taught him to surrender to Vakratunda, Brahman everywhere, neither god-only nor demon-only lord. Angry demons abandon him and return home. Joyful Dambha and Kāvya go outside to Gaṇeśa, prostrate, worship and hymn his Brahman, yoga, impartial, elephant-faced/Siddhi-Buddhi-lord forms. He falls again; Gaṇeśa raises him.
outcome: Dambha surrenders with his guru; army declines to accompany him.

details: Gaṇeśa promises Dambha’s hymn joy, family/wealth/grain, relief of mental/physical affliction and troubles; regular once/twice/thrice-daily recitation pleases him. He came to kill but spares the surrendered devotee. Dambha requests firm devotion, instructions for livelihood and a stable place. Siddhibuddhipati grants unwavering devotion and own-station residence without fear for a long time; gods are not higher nor Dambha lower, all pleasing when faithful to own duty. Dambha must destroy undertakings begun without remembrance, make ritual actions fruitless without first worship, and protect beloved devotees free of Dambha disposition; acts lacking initial remembrance/worship become his karma-share.
outcome: Survival, devotion and conditional obstruction/protection duties replace battle.

details: Gaṇeśa disappears after assigning Dambha’s duties. Gods/sages acclaim victory and return radiant and fearless to their own stations; demons dwell untroubled in Pātāla cavities. Mudgala concludes Dambha’s pacification and Brahmā-sonhood and promises attentive listeners/tellers freedom from Dambha fear, Brahman, desired objects, prosperity and freedom from obstacles. He explicitly transitions to Vāmana.
outcome: Divine offices restored and demons peacefully resident; next arc is Vāmana.

details: Dakṣa asks Vāmana’s story. Mudgala introduces Kaśyapa, his senior virtuous wife Aditi, and gods including Indra born to them; opposing demons are also sage’s sons, defeated by Viṣṇu’s varied forms. They seek Kāvya, who advises100 Aśvamedhas with concealed hostility, making Bali Indra and demons celestial enjoyers. Bali, born of Virocana, is Viṣṇu-devoted and dislikes adharma. Yet he begins the first sacrifice remembering Viṣṇu and omitting Gaṇeśa. Vighna decides to consume its ritual fruits, enters Indra’s heart; Indra fears100 sacrifices will replace him and asks Viṣṇu to destroy them. Vighna then enters Viṣṇu’s heart as time-form.
outcome: Neglected initial worship creates obstruction through the divine opponents.

details: Viṣṇu tells Indra that Aditi and Kaśyapa previously worshipped him intensely for100 years and requested his sonhood; he agreed and will fulfil it now to stop Bali’s sacrifice. Forgetting Bali’s devotion, Viṣṇu is born Vāmana to Kaśyapa in Aditi, but cannot displace mighty Bali. He asks father Kaśyapa for means; receives Vakratunda’s six-syllable mantra, goes to Vidarbha and worships foodless for10 years, meditating Gaṇeśa. Vakratunda appears through mantra/austerity, lion-mounted, four-armed, one-tusked, elephant-faced, red, with Siddhi/Buddhi and noose/goad. Vāmana rises, bows and begins hymn.
outcome: Vāmana seeks Gaṇeśa’s aid after initial inability to move Bali.

details: Vāmana hymns Vakratunda as obstacle remover/giver, indwelling lord, and eminent forms including Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Indra, sun, moon, Yama, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Kubera, Agni, Nirṛti, Śeṣa, Śukra, Sanatkumāra and Guha. He dances with tears and horripilation, losing body-awareness in exclusive devotion. Pleased deity offers wishes, promises hymn siddhi, desired objects and final Svānanda liberation. Vāmana requests firm devotion, Bali brought within his power, the deity’s appearance whenever remembered, and freedom from obstruction. Gaṇeśa agrees and disappears; Vāmana installs him, establishing Adoṣa field in Vidarbha.
outcome: All requested granted, with deity installed at Adoṣa.

details: After worshipping Vakratunda and bowing to Kaśyapa, Vāmana reaches Bali’s sacrifice. Sages marvel at radiant short Vedic student; Bali rises, bows, worships and offers a gift. Śukra understands purpose and the initial worship omission producing a Viṣṇu-form obstacle. Vāmana asks land for three steps; Bali grants with devotion. Remembering Gaṇeśa, Vāmana becomes Virāṭ, covers heaven with one step and earth with second, demands place for third. Grieving Bali cannot answer; angry Viṣṇu binds him as debtor to a Brahmin and tells him to go to Naraka. Bali realizes his Gaṇeśa omission has brought this treatment even from his chosen Viṣṇu, and turns to Gaṇeśa for rescue.
outcome: Bali is bound for unfulfilled third step, then seeks Gaṇeśa.

details: Bali hymns Gaṇeśa as obstacle lord, all-form/impartial Brahman, Siddhi-Buddhi lord and māyā-remover; confesses own pride/envy and repeated offences, asks protection from falling into Naraka, and explains refuge gives gods freedom from illusion/obstacles. A sky-voice promises surrendered Bali no fear of Naraka through remembrance. His hymn frees readers/hearers of that fear, grants four aims and increases devotion; joyful Bali keeps meditating.
outcome: Bali receives explicit protection from Naraka before debt is discharged.

details: Vighna leaves Viṣṇu, immediately restoring understanding. Vāmana realizes he harmed his full devotee Bali and a Brahmin debt could send him to Naraka; he seeks Gaṇeśa and remembers him. Gaṇeśa appears immediately, receives worship from Viṣṇu and gods/sages. Gaining insight from the sight, Bali offers his body and asks the third foot placed on his head. Viṣṇu agrees, discharging the Brahmin debt, and begins hymn with assembly.
outcome: Both understand; third-step head gift discharges debt.

details: Vāmana hymns Gaṇeśa’s supremacy/māyā, begs forgiveness and sacrificial fruit for Bali, acknowledging Bali’s belief in Viṣṇu’s superiority led to omitted worship. Gaṇeśa says he had earlier promised Naraka through Viṣṇu’s hands, but now Bali has taken bodily/mental/verbal refuge and Viṣṇu also petitions. He orders finishing sacrifice with him first; Bali thereby gains all sacrifices’ fruit, but current fruitlessness lets him experience offence. Bali will be Indra after current Indra retires; for now establish him in Pātāla. All approve; Bali completes the final sacrifice placing Gaṇeśa first. Deity vanishes, gods return home; hearing the arc grants wishes.
outcome: Sacrifice repaired; Pātāla placement ordered and future Indra office promised.

details: Vyāsa answers Janamejaya: Ruru’s son Durgama, of Hiraṇyākṣa’s family, plans to obtain Vedas so gods lose offerings. He worships Brahmā in the Himalaya for1,000years on air. Brahmā offers a boon; Durgama requests all Vedic mantras of gods/Brahmins and conquering strength; Brahmā agrees.
outcome: Brahmins forget Vedas and Vedic rites cease.

details: Without Vedic rites gods weaken. Durgama attacks Amarāvatī; gods flee into Sumeru caves. Rain ceases for100years, drying water and killing people and animals. Brahmins fast and pray to the Mother in the Himalaya.
outcome: The Goddess answers the petition.

details: The Goddess appears with innumerable eyes and four arms holding bow, arrows, lotus and food. She weeps for nine nights, restoring water; many-eyed Śatākṣī distributes vegetables, roots and fruits until crops return, and grass for animals, receiving the designation Śākambharī.
outcome: Famine relief precedes the battle.

details: Messengers tell Durgama of the rescue; he surrounds the defenders with1,000akṣauhiṇīs. A luminous enclosure protects gods and Brahmins while the Goddess fights outside. Arrow clouds darken the sky; frictional fire illuminates it. Fourteen named Śaktis,10,000Guhya Kālikās, groups of32and64and innumerable others emerge and fight.
outcome: After the Śaktis destroy100akṣauhiṇīs, instruments sound and Durgama first confronts them; ten days of fighting destroy all his troops.

details: On day11 red-clothed Durgama advances in his chariot, overcomes Śaktis and faces the Goddess for two praharas. Her15arrows strike four horses, charioteer, two eyes, two arms, flag, and five strike his heart. He vomits blood and dies; his luminosity merges into the Goddess.
outcome: Durgama dies; this is no surrender.

details: Gods including Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva praise the victor. She hands the Vedas to the Brahmins and instructs that they be guarded as parts of her body. She connects Durgā with killing Durgama and names Durgā/Śatākṣī remembrance as liberating from Māyā; the many-eye naming explanation occurred earlier. She enjoins both Suras and Asuras to serve her alone and read her deeds, then disappears. Vyāsa directs secrecy for this mystery and promises daily devoted hearing fulfills wishes and ends in honor in Devī Loka.
outcome: Vedic possession restored; story closes.

details: Aruṇa lives in a nether Daitya city, then undertakes Brahmā worship beside Ganges in Himalaya. Four successive10,000year stages use dry leaves, water drops, air and finally no food; he repeats Gāyatrī continuously. His ascetic heat threatens worlds; gods petition Brahmā. Brahmā appears with Gāyatrī and four Vedas.
outcome: Brahmā offers a boon.

details: Aruṇa first requests immortality. Brahmā refuses an impossible boon and says Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva too are mortal. Aruṇa revises the request to the specified war/weapon/sex/limb-category death exclusions and strength to conquer gods. Brahmā assents.
outcome: A qualified boon, not universal immortality, is granted.

details: Aruṇa gathers nether Daityas, sends a messenger to Indra and conquers heaven, taking forms/offices of sun, moon, Yama, Agni and others through ascetic power. Gods seek counsel with Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva at Kailāsa.
outcome: Gods cannot readily defeat him.

details: A heavenly voice directs worship of the world Queen and identifies cessation of Gāyatrī repetition as the condition making Aruṇa killable. Indra sends Bṛhaspati; gods perform Devī sacrifice and Māyā-bīja worship. Bṛhaspati approaches as a muni and argues that sharing the gods’ Goddess worship undermines Aruṇa’s hostility. Aruṇa abandons Gāyatrī through pride and loses strength; Bṛhaspati reports success.
outcome: Gods continue worship; a long interval of unspecified duration follows.

details: After continued worship Bhrāmarī appears with diverse garments and ornaments, bees in her fists and garland, and boon/fearlessness gestures. Bee sound is associated with Hrīm. Gods offer an extended hymn, then describe Aruṇa’s boon and injuries. Hymnic names are attributed praise, not separate narrated births.
outcome: Bhrāmarī responds to their crisis.

details: Bhrāmarī releases bees/hornets from every side. Their multitude covers the world and attacks the Daityas’ chests. The text denies the foes time or capacity to fight, wield weapons or speak; principal Daityas perish immediately. Bees return to the Goddess; gods rejoice with praise, music and dance.
outcome: Aruṇa’s forces perish; no negotiated surrender.

details: The Goddess grants separate boons to the gods, whose individual contents are not specified here, and grants their express request for unshakeable devotion. She disappears; Nārāyaṇa concludes with liberation promised for hearing the account.
outcome: Narrative closes.

details: Gods distressed after Satī’s departure and by Tāraka worship the Goddess. They report Brahmā’s provision that Śiva’s son kills Tāraka, and request her incarnation and steadfast devotion. She promises that her Śakti will be Gaurī in Himālaya’s house, Śiva’s wife and mother of the slayer. These are promises here, not a birth already narrated. Himālaya praises the favor and asks for her Vedāntic true nature and knowledge with devotion.
outcome: Goddess begins teaching at7.31.74.

details: The Goddess identifies her precreation self with consciousness and Brahman and describes inherent Māyā, its concealment and liberation functions, and dependence of cosmos on her Śakti. The discourse moves through elements, subtle/causal/gross bodies, organs and prāṇas, and Jīva/Īśvara distinctions. This is attributed doctrine; translator parenthetical explanations and potentially corrupt organ locations need Sanskrit checking.
outcome: Teaching continues in7.33 onward.

details: Vyāsa answers with the Goddess’s own created residence, Maṇidvīpa, above the other divine worlds and serving as an umbrella over them. Sudhā ocean surrounds it; the outer iron enclosure is seven yojanas, with four guarded gates receiving divine visitors and vehicles. The next enclosure is white copper in this English witness.
outcome: Further gardens, seasonal rulers and enclosures follow.

details: The opening invokes Gaṇeśa as complete yoga, giver of siddhis, heart-resident of yogins, the human/elephant form with attributed human and attribute-free elephant aspects; salutations include Śiva, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Śakti, Brahmā, Śeṣa, Nara and Nārāyaṇa and the gods, yogins and sages.
outcome: Invocations establish the local teaching frame.

details: Fearful of Kali faults and instructed by Brahmā, Śaunaka and other sages reside at Naimiṣa with Vedic study, five sacrifices and daily/occasional duties. Sūta arrives, marvels at their conduct, bows, praises the sight of their feet as liberating, and accepts their offered seat and reciprocal welcome.
outcome: Sūta is seated as narrator.

details: Śaunaka calls Vyāsa an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, divider of Veda and Purāṇas; Sūta learned Purāṇas and histories from him. Requested to recite, Sūta credits his teacher and tells many accounts and doctrines associated with the four human aims; the listeners rejoice.
outcome: Many narratives have been heard before the present question.

details: Hearing differing accounts that call Śiva, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Śakti, Gaṇeśa, Virāj, Brahman, yoga, knowledge, action, self, breath, food, mind, intellect, Sāṃkhya or Svānanda supreme leaves the sages uncertain. Śaunaka asks for one scripturally accepted conclusion; Sūta introduces Mudgala’s teaching as that essence.
outcome: The Mudgala–Dakṣa frame is introduced.

details: Sūta briefly previews the ruined sacrifice: Rudra’s forces defeat gods, Vīrabhadra beheads Dakṣa, Brahmā conciliates Śiva and Śiva revives Dakṣa through yoga. Distressed and curse-confused Dakṣa receives the Gaṇeśa devotee Mudgala, addresses him as Āṅgirasa and asks help; Mudgala tells him to remember Vighnarāja.
outcome: The damaged Dakṣa seeks instruction; chapters2–4 retrospectively explain this outcome.

details: Dakṣa says the curse erased his knowledge and office; Mudgala’s presence brings some awareness and prompts his questions about Vighnapati. The sages request the cause. Sūta says Dakṣa is one of Brahmā’s ten sons and was made chief of Prajāpatis, then became proud.
outcome: Pride in office precedes the insult.

details: At Śiva’s Kailāsa assembly, Viṣṇu sits left, Brahmā right, Nandin-led Gaṇas nearby; Vasiṣṭha praises, Nārada-led singers sing, Apsarases dance. Śiva greets Dakṣa verbally but does not bow. Dakṣa invokes his father-in-law status, treats Śiva as son-like, denounces Śiva’s conduct and appearance, and ignores Brahmā’s rebuke.
outcome: Dakṣa’s hostile speech provokes Nandin.

details: Nandikeśvara condemns the slander, says Śiva plays with māyā without its faults, and curses Dakṣa to lose knowledge, obtain a goat face through the mouth that slandered Śiva, and lose his kingdom.
outcome: Nandin announces the curse conditions and outcomes.

details: Dakṣa replies that Śiva’s followers lack proper conduct and curses Śaivas to ignorance, Kali-age heterodoxy, matted hair, nakedness, ash, indulgence and hell. Brahmā rebukes him; Dakṣa leaves angry, the assembly disperses unhappy and Śiva is distressed. The precise study-related clause at42 is separately retained as unresolved.
outcome: Mutual curses and dispersal close the assembly episode.

details: Sūta frames non-devotion to Vighneśa as the cause of obstruction. At home Dakṣa wants to humble Śiva. Nārada recommends Bṛhaspatisava excluding Śiva’s sacrificial share; Dakṣa adopts it. Viṣṇu, gods, Gandharvas, Brahmins and Kaśyapa-led sons-in-law with wives gather. Both Gaṇeśa and Śiva are excluded, and all forget Gaṇeśa amid coming pride.
outcome: An exclusionary Bṛhaspatisava begins.

details: Dadhīci warns that a sacrifice without Śiva is like a lifeless body. Dakṣa rejects him, appealing to Viṣṇu’s presence. Dadhīci foretells ruin, curses attendees to Kali-age heterodoxy and loss of duty ending in hell, curses Viṣṇu to supporting heterodox followers, and predicts divine defeat and sage distress. Dadhīci leaves with Gautama, Gālava, Vāmadeva, Dvita, Trita, Mārkaṇḍeya and Agastya; Viṣṇu consoles remaining attendees, and Bhṛgu-led sages proceed.
outcome: Śaiva sages depart; the remaining sacrifice proceeds.

details: Nārada goes to Kailāsa, asks Satī why she has not joined the festival where her sisters and their husbands rejoice, and says honor/dishonor is irrelevant in a father’s or husband’s home. Satī asks Śiva to accompany her. He warns that her father hates him and has not invited him, offering instead a local sacrifice if she creates sages/gods. She asks leave; he remains silent. She decides permission is unnecessary and leaves; amazed Śiva sends a vimāna accepting what will occur.
outcome: Satī goes despite warning and absence of explicit permission.

details: Satī arrives by vimāna and is welcomed by mother, father, sisters and kin. Dakṣa welcomes her; she objects that she came uninvited. He blames his mistaken marriage arrangement made on his father’s advice and Śiva’s faults, while asking her to remain. Seeing no Rudra share and hearing slander, she declares the rite fruitless and renounces the body derived from Dakṣa.
outcome: Satī rejects her paternal body after repeated slander.

details: Satī meditates on Śiva in her heart, burns her body with yoga-fire and reaches the divine abode. The narrator then says the goddess by her own māyā becomes Himācala’s daughter, meditates and performs severe austerity, and again obtains Śiva as husband as Pārvatī.
outcome: After body abandonment, chapter3 anticipates rebirth and remarriage in an advance narrator summary. Chapter4 returns to Śiva’s earlier response to the death, before that predicted birth.

details: Śiva waits under the banyan with Nandin and yogins; omens disturb them. Nārada praises Satī’s body-burning; his silence to the death question makes Śiva understand. Śiva grieves, calls himself powerless without Śakti, recalls pride in inseparable Ardhanārīśvara lordship and realizes he had failed to remember Vighnarāja.
outcome: Grief becomes recognition of pride and neglected Gaṇeśa worship.

details: Śiva meditates on a four-armed, elephant-faced, great-bodied, large-bellied Gaṇeśa wearing crown, earrings, gem-garland, navel Śeṣa, anklets and chest Cintāmaṇi, with Siddhi/Buddhi. His hymn calls Gaṇeśa obstacle-creator for non-devotees and remover for devotees, cosmic creator of guṇa-linked Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva, and Svānanda resident. He asks restoration of capacity to act, stating he cannot even walk without Śakti.
outcome: Śiva petitions for restored power to act.

details: Gaṇeśa appears, attributes the obstruction to Śiva’s pride, and approves renewed remembrance and praise. He promises Śakti’s rebirth as Himācala’s daughter and remarriage as Satī/Pārvatī, Śiva’s empowered lordship through devotion/grace, and immediate appearance whenever Śiva remembers him; then disappears.
outcome: Śiva receives future reunion and present restoration of agency.

details: Restored to action and remembering Gaṇeśa, Śiva strikes his matted hair. Vīrabhadra arises with three heads, three feet and trident, bows as servant, receives the command to destroy Dakṣa and the sacrifice, laughs so the three worlds tremble, and creates innumerable Rudras from his body. Nandin-led Śiva Gaṇas follow.
outcome: Vīrabhadra and his generated Rudras march to the sacrifice.

details: Omens terrify sacrifice attendees. Vīrabhadra, Rudras, Nandin, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Bhṛṅgin and Puṣpadanta attack; attendants flee, the pavilion is broken, gods/sages are beaten, wives are seized/beaten and taunted over husbands’ Śiva hostility, offerings eaten and altar defiled.
outcome: The sacrificial order is violently disrupted.

details: Śiva enters with bow/arrows and fights: he breaks Pūṣan’s teeth and removes Bhaga’s eyes. Nandin seizes Dharma, Bhṛṅgin Kaśyapa, Puṣpadanta beats Varuṇa, Bhairava seizes/fells Indra, Vīrabhadra fells Dakṣa. Viṣṇu fights and hurts Rudra/ghost forces; Śiva remembers Gaṇeśa and wounds Viṣṇu’s heart with arrows, felling him.
outcome: Viṣṇu is felled by Śiva’s heart-directed arrows; recovery is narrated in the following event.

details: Recovering, Viṣṇu releases the destructive Nārāyaṇa missile; Śiva releases Pāśupata. They fight in the sky and generate fire threatening earth and three worlds. Meanwhile Vīrabhadra treats Dakṣa as a sacrificial beast, cuts his head and offers it into fire. Viṣṇu hurls the cakra, which bows to Śiva and stops rather than striking him.
outcome: Dakṣa is beheaded; the cakra fails to attack Śiva.

details: Śiva raises his trident to kill Viṣṇu, but an unidentified heavenly voice forbids it and commands protection; Brahmā arrives, praises Śiva, warns against untimely destruction, and reconciles him with ashamed bowing Viṣṇu. Brahmā offers remaining oblations as Rudra’s share and asks restoration/restart. Śiva restores Bhaga’s eyes, makes Pūṣan a eater of ground food, and restores gods/sages/wives/servants to forms and radiance.
outcome: Viṣṇu survives and attendees are restored.

details: Because Dakṣa’s head was burnt, Śiva orders Bhṛṅgin to kill the first being he sees and bring its head. Bhṛṅgin sees a goat, kills it, brings its head; Śiva attaches it and revives Dakṣa. Brahmā prompts the now-humble Dakṣa to praise Śiva.
outcome: Dakṣa rises alive with a goat head.

details: Dakṣa’s hymn identifies Śiva with time-governed cosmic processes and asks pardon for pride. His goat-like speech delights Śiva, who restores his former human head, promises restored recognized Prajāpati chiefship, desired gifts and Śiva’s world to hymn-praisers, and fulfillment to one making the goat-like sound before him once. Śiva disappears, others return home, but Dakṣa remains distressed; the narrator explains temple bleating practice.
outcome: Human head and office restored; Dakṣa’s remaining distress leads to Mudgala teaching.

details: Mudgala calls Gaṇeśa universal mother/father and first-worshipped Jyeṣṭharāja/Vināyaka, resident in Svānanda; all others are his partial expressions. Pride in self-supremacy brings obstruction and lost office; contemplative recognition brings refuge and relief. Cintāmaṇi is explained as illuminator of mind’s five operations. Mudgala urges Dakṣa’s refuge; Dakṣa asks how to know/worship him.
outcome: A nested Śiva–Pārvatī teaching is requested.

details: At Kailāsa Pārvatī asks why universally honored Śiva meditates, knowing none above him. Śiva says he meditates day/night on heart-resident Svānanda Gaṇeśa beyond form/formlessness and mental/speech opposition. Pārvatī asks how such meditation works, adopts a disciple’s position and seeks realization; Śiva accepts her fitness for this path.
outcome: Pārvatī explicitly becomes a requesting disciple.

details: Dakṣa asks Mudgala to continue. Remembering Gaṇeśa, Śiva distinguishes mind-apprehended māyā from what transcends it, explains self-aware Svānanda and Cintāmaṇi’s illumination of five mental grounds, and says Gaṇeśa can be contemplated through non-separation yoga. Pārvatī says the compressed teaching is not understood and requests an easier detailed account of māyā-bound and transcendent Brahman; Śiva begins.
outcome: The question leads directly into creation teaching.

details: Śiva begins after praising Pārvatī’s Gaṇeśa interest. The teaching traces Brahman, self/other emergence and reflection, māyā as Buddhi and deluding Siddhi, illuminated by Gaṇeśa. Desire to become many yields body/embodied forms described as bindu and so’ham; these two cannot perform their functions without efficacy.
outcome: The future Prakṛti/Puruṣa pair lacks power to act.

details: The two perform severe austerity to their own true form for1,000 divine years. Gaṇeśa appears with trunk, large belly/ears, four arms and three eyes. Recognition lets them bow and hymn: formless trunk and formed body below neck, four arms explained through avyakta/sama/sat/asat principles, belly containing all, and feet through māyā/māyika. They ask him to remain in their heart, specify what duty to perform, and give intense devotion.
outcome: Prakṛti/Puruṣa ask direction and devotion.

details: Gaṇeśa grants their wishes and declares hymn rewards: four aims, nourishment, release from jail at100,000 recitations, destruction of harmful rites, desired fruit at21recitations for21days, and Brahmanhood for desireless reading. He names Prakṛti as source of creation, grants unbound devotion and gifts to her desireful/desireless devotees. Puruṣa receives so’ham identity, unbound devotion, grant-giving and yogic Brahmanhood-bestowal; he must implant efficacy-seed in Prakṛti for world creation. Creation, maintenance and destruction proceed at due times; they are called universal mother/father. Gaṇeśa disappears and they obey.
outcome: Cosmic duties and devotional grants enable subsequent creation.

details: Pārvatī asks what follows the divine disappearance. Śiva says Prakṛti and Puruṣa gain capacity and mutual affinity; she enchants him, he plants seed, she becomes pregnant and later gives birth to luminous Mahān/Mahat, eldest among tattvas and their inner principle.
outcome: Mahat is born in the explicitly cosmological genealogy.

details: Mahat creates Ahaṃkāra, divided into sattva/rajas/tamas and knowledge/action/material powers. The tamasic sequence produces sound/space, touch/wind, form/fire, taste/water, smell/earth and a five-element body. The text’s conceptual generation is preserved as Śiva’s cosmogony.
outcome: Ahaṃkāra’s three powers generate subtle/elemental structure.

details: Rājasic power creates sensory organs tongue/eye/skin/nose/ear, action organs hands/feet/anus/speech/generative organ and five breaths prāṇa/vyāna/apāna/udāna/samāna. Sāttvic power creates sensory deities directions/Vāyu/Varuṇa/Aśvins/Sūrya and action deities Agni/Viṣṇu/Prajāpāla/Indra/Mitra; lists are retained without inventing one-to-one mappings.
outcome: Ten listed presiding deities and functional organs appear.

details: The primordial tattva deities lack knowledge and cannot create. Prakṛti and Puruṣa give the one-syllable Gaṇeśa mantra with ritual procedure. Severe austerity of unspecified duration wins appearance. Their hymn addresses Vakratunda through opposed theological pairs and describes noose/goad/tusk/abhaya, four arms, large ears/belly, one tusk and elephant face. They stand ready for his answer.
outcome: Teachers and mantra lead to manifestation and hymn.

details: Gaṇeśa offers their desired boon and promises hymn hearers/readers siddhis, knowledge, wealth, wife, good sons, liberation and victory as requested. Ādiṛṣis/tattvas ask unwavering devotion, creative capacity, ability to give devotees siddhis, fulfillment and perpetual freedom from bondage. Gaṇeśa explicitly grants all requests and disappears.
outcome: The tattvas receive the requested compound boon.

details: After sorrow at disappearance, boon-enlightened tattvas mutually interpenetrate and form an egg. Guṇeśa arises within, emits waters, grows full-bodied and splits the egg by radiance; his universal limbs, cosmic pores, fourth/mahākāraṇa state and lordship of guṇas are described. Activity produces names Nārāyaṇa/Brahma/Mahādeva/Sūrya/Ādiśakti in this cosmic explanation, not automatic identity with each separately established actor. Ignorance prompts severe Gaṇeśa meditation and one-syllable japa over an unspecified long time; Gaṇeśa appears and offers a boon.
outcome: Guṇeśa emerges and becomes a boon petitioner.

details: Guṇeśa hymns Gaṇeśa as tranquil yoga lord through form/without-form and various cosmic/doctrinal descriptions, distinguishing those as partial manifestations. He calls sight/tapas fruitful and requests firm devotion destroying delusion, creative capacity, fulfilling devotees’ wishes and unobstructed works.
outcome: Requested devotion and creative power are explicit.

details: Gaṇeśa grants devotion, varied creation without obstruction, gift-giving, and his appearance when a great task arises. Guṇeśa’s hymn is named Stutisāraka, promising Brahmanhood/siddhis, desires to desireful users and liberation to desireless devotees; three-times-daily reading makes Gaṇeśa attainable. He disappears; Guṇeśa feels separation.
