outcome: The creative boon is granted; Guṇeśa’s next actions begin9.

details: Boon-enlightened Guṇeśa turns to creation. Vedas emerge from his breath; he creates the equal-element causal sleep-state world called Pradhāna, tamasic and ignorant of duty. It performs1,000divine-year tapas, receives Gaṇeśa’s appearance, worships/praises and gets yogic capacity. Vedas independently perform severe tapas and worship: Ṛg uses Brahmaṇaspati-sūkta, Yajus Gaṇeśa-śānti, Sāman eight-name praise, Atharvan Atharvaśīrṣa. Gaṇeśa grants universal teacher-standing, accepted/praised worldwide.
outcome: Pradhāna and Vedas receive differentiated powers.

details: Asked what Pradhāna does, Śiva says it creates subtle sāttvic Hiraṇyagarbha/dream world, enclosed by subtle principles. Lacking knowledge, Hiraṇyagarbha performs difficult tapas and receives the desired, unspecified boon/capacity. It creates gross rājasic waking world; this also lacks knowledge, performs tapas, receives appearance, worships and gains a boon/capacity. Gross world becomes many three-state worlds; innumerable eggs emerge from Guṇeśa’s pores. The enclosing/enclosed unity is called Prakṛti/Brahma-bindu.
outcome: Causal→subtle→gross creation proceeds through distinct tapas/boons.

details: Gross waking creates space, then wind, fire, water and earth with sound/touch/form/taste/smell. Mutual entering gives earth5qualities, water4,fire3,wind2,space1. Prakṛti has eight envelope forms empowered by reflected Guṇeśa; Virāṭ arises in the egg. Earth’s displayed extent is50crore and successive envelopes are tenfold:water/fire/wind/space/waking-ego/dream-Mahat/sleep-māyā. Final order encloses Virāṭ by earth, earth by water, water by fire, fire by wind, wind by space, space by ego, ego by Mahat, Mahat by māyā. Countless such eggs surround Guṇeśa.
outcome: The eight-envelope egg and its cosmic inhabitant are established.

details: Pārvatī asks Virāṭ’s form. Śiva describes5croreyojana body and14worlds:feet Pātāla,ankles Rasātala,heels Mahātala,shanks Talātala,knees Sutala,thighs Vitala,waist-junction Atala,waist Bhūloka,navel Bhuvar,heart Svar,neck Mahar,mouth Jana,forehead Tapo,head Satya. Thousands of heads/faces/feet/hands/ears/bellies and universal pervasion are described, with external waking Vaiśvānara, inner dream Hiraṇyagarbha, sleep-state Īśvara and fourth self-state.
outcome: Virāṭ body-world and state correspondences are established.

details: Ignorant Virāṭ meditates in his heart with the one-syllable procedure and performs1,000divine-year severe tapas. Gaṇeśa appears and offers a boon. Virāṭ bows, credits sight with fulfilled birth/tapas/knowledge/body, and hymns the deity through Siddhi/Buddhi lordship, cosmic deity forms, māyā/transcendent qualities and source-of-knowledge powers.
outcome: Virāṭ petitions through worship and praise.

details: Gaṇeśa declares hymn rewards of siddhi, desired gifts and enjoyment/liberation for faithful reading/hearing. Virāṭ asks firm devotion destroying delusion, capacity for creation/preservation/destruction, unequaled lordship and fulfillment. Gaṇeśa says so be it and disappears; Virāṭ happily contemplates him. Śiva says other cosmic eggs’ Virāṭs likewise perform tapas and receive unobstructed duties, while cosmic eggs are innumerable.
outcome: Virāṭ’s compound cosmic boon is granted.

details: Pārvatī asks Virāṭ’s creation and meditation method; Dakṣa asks Mudgala to continue. Śiva says Virāṭ remembers Gaṇeśa and creates Brahmā from navel,Viṣṇu from mouth,Hara from eye,Śakti/Pārvatī from left side,Sūrya from right. Ignorant of self and origin, five wander long in darkness, then contemplate whatever is the root and undertake severe tapas. Gaṇeśa enters inwardly, giving heart-vision of a one-syllable seed-mantra; japa brings pure knowledge.
outcome: Five receive the inwardly revealed mantra rather than an invented external guru.

details: After1,000divine years Gaṇeśa manifests with immeasurable solar radiance,trunk,four arms,large belly,adornments/weapons,Siddhi/Buddhi and mouse vehicle. The five fear burning and call on Vighneśa; he makes his form gentle, giving perception and recognition. They hymn names including Heramba/Dhundhirāja/Vināyaka and opposed cosmic/yogic states, seek protection and fall silent.
outcome: Fright is relieved by a gentle form and knowledge.

details: Gaṇeśa offers their desired boon and hymn fruits:four aims,sons/grandsons,prosperity,final Svānanda; prison release at7dailyrecitations for21days; divine honor from1/2/3times-dailyreading; no fear of harmful rites at21recitations for21days; wealth/grain,health,cattle and desired ends. The five ask firm devotion preventing māyā-affliction,direction,varied power,devotee wish fulfillment and a place of perpetual bliss.
outcome: The common request precedes individual cosmic assignments.

details: Gaṇeśa grants individual roles:four-faced rājasic Brahmā creates,lives Satyaloka and rides haṃsa with Vedic knowledge;four-armed sāttvic Viṣṇu preserves,lives Vaikuṇṭha,rides Garuḍa and has many incarnations;five-faced tāmasic Hara destroys,lives Kailāsa,rides bull and burns all by third eye;thousand-rayed Sūrya activates karma/six seasons,is planet-king,rain-root,resides Sauraloka and rides a horse-adorned chariot;four-armed Śakti/Mahāmāyā deludes through enjoyment/liberation,resides Śaktiloka and rides lion. Gaṇeśa promises appearance at great tasks,grants weapons/ornaments,varied capacities and fulfilled resolve,and disappears. Five rejoice as empowered wish-fulfillers. At1.11.75 Gaṇeśa also declares the gods made equal to himself in all respects; this is attributed grant speech, without inferred unconditional invulnerability.
outcome: Five cosmic functions,stations,mounts and powers are assigned.

cause: Mukundā’s desire persists after the real prince’s departure.
details: Vyāsa asks about Mukundā after hearing Rukmāṅgada’s ascent. She remains consumed by desire, abandons food/water and sleeps exhausted in the forest. Indra knows her longing, assumes Rukmāṅgada’s form and has intercourse with her; she returns home believing the prince was her partner. Indra vanishes. She conceives and bears a beautiful son in the ninth month.
outcome: Impersonation yields pregnancy; her belief is explicitly mistaken.

cause: Vācaknavi believes the child belongs to his household.
details: Birth resounds through earth, sky and directions and startles birds. Vācaknavi leaves his daily rites and, unaware of Mukundā’s conduct, joyfully performs birth rites and donations. After ten days he names the child Gṛtsamada with astrologer Brahmin approval; in the fifth year initiates him and performs four Vedic vows. The boy learns from a single utterance. Vācaknavi, called father in this social/ritual setting, teaches the Vedic Gaṇānāṃ tvā mantra, prescribing steady Gaṇeśa contemplation for success and fame.
outcome: Naming, initiation, learning and mantra instruction completed.

cause: Boast during learned discussion produces parentage rebuke.
details: Gṛtsamada practices mantra/meditation. King Magadha of Magadha, generous, martial and learned, with two unnamed learned ministers and devoted curse/grace-capable wife Ambikā, hosts his father’s śrāddha. Invited sages include Vasiṣṭha and Atri, and Gṛtsamada. His boast in śāstra discussion provokes Atri’s rebuke: ascetic merit earns respect, but alleged birth from prince Rukmāṅgada excludes equal sage-honour. Gṛtsamada flares with rage, others flee, and he threatens to burn the sages by curse if he proves not Rukmāṅgada’s son.
outcome: He leaves to interrogate his mother; alleged parentage is attributed speech.

cause: Alleged excluded lineage causes confrontation.
details: Gṛtsamada demands his father’s identity and threatens to burn Mukundā if she refuses. Frightened, she admits longing for the hunting prince while husband Vācaknavi was practicing, and believes Rukmāṅgada his father. Ashamed and angry, the son curses her to be a thorny forest plant with countless fruits shunned by all living creatures.
outcome: Mother receives curse; her father-identification remains attributed mistaken belief.

cause: Mother responds to curse with countercurse.
details: Mukundā counters that her son disregarded motherhood: he will father a terrible mighty daitya frightening three worlds. She immediately abandons her body and becomes a forest badarī avoided even by birds. Heavenly speech reveals Gṛtsamada was born from Indra. He leaves for austerity. Hearing this account promises freedom from distress and fulfilment.
outcome: Plant transformation realized; true paternity revealed; future-son promise remains future.

cause: Parentage humiliation drives intense austerity.
details: Gṛtsamada reaches flower-rich Puṣpaka forest, bows to resident sages and stays with permission. Bathing, he fixes mind on Gaṇeśa, stands on a toe, restrains senses/breath/self, looks toward nose-tip and takes air. After1,000 divine years, opened eyes emit fire distressing gods who fear whose office he seeks. He then subsists on one fallen leaf, immobile, for a further15,000 as stated (the later clause gives number without repeating years).
outcome: Long austerity and emitted fire draw divine attention.

cause: Compassion rewards rigorous austerity.
details: Compassionate Gaṇeśa appears quickly, radiant, moon-browed, lion-mounted, ten-armed with serpent sacred cord and lotus garland, accompanied by Siddhi/Buddhi. His radiance overwhelms Gṛtsamada, who faints, resumes inward contemplation and fears his practice wasted; he begs rescue and recalls exclusion from sage honours. Gaṇeśa identifies himself as arriving for grace, praises toe-supported austerity and asks desired boon. The sage bows joyfully.
outcome: Overwhelming vision becomes understood as grace, enabling request.

cause: Divine boon invitation.
details: Weeping and dancing, Gṛtsamada calls birth/austerity fulfilled. By deity’s command he asks Brahman-knowledge and knowledge, firm devotion and unforgetting remembrance, supremacy among devotees, exclusive devotional standing able to draw three worlds, worldwide honour by gods/humans. He asks Puṣpaka forest/city fame as Gaṇeśapura, continued divine residence and fulfilment of devotees’ wishes.
outcome: Personal knowledge/devotion/honour and site requests articulated.

cause: Knowledge/devotion/site requests receive personal reply.
details: Gaṇeśa affirms all requested things and grants rare Brahmin standing. Because he recited Gaṇānāṃ tvā, Gṛtsamada becomes that Vedic mantra’s ṛṣi; he gains supreme honour before Brahmā and Vasiṣṭha’s sages. Remembering him first then Gaṇeśa at undertakings yields success; ritual without deity/ṛṣi/metre knowledge is fruitless. A mighty famous son will terrify gods, be undefeatable by all except Rudra and remain Gaṇeśa-devoted. Site names are Puṣpaka in divine/Kṛta era as printed devayuga, Maṇipūra in Tretā, Bhānaka in Dvāpara and Bhadraka in Kali; bathing/giving there grants wishes.
outcome: Personal and ritual standing granted; future son specified with Rudra exception.

cause: Boon site request is realized through installation.
details: Gaṇeśa vanishes after giving boons. Gṛtsamada installs his image, builds a fine temple, establishes enduring Varada name and worships devotedly. Site becomes a siddhi-place/Puṣpaka through divine favour. Listening to boon-account promises all wishes and firm Gaṇeśa devotion freeing transmigration.
outcome: Actual temple, named cult image and worship close recognition/site arc.

cause: Divine son promise follows Gṛtsamada recognition.
details: Vyāsa asks Gṛtsamada’s later conduct. Sages now honour/select him for sacrifices and remember him at Gaṇeśa worship, fulfilling recognition. Still devoted, he sneezes mightily and sees a radiant red fearsome child. Initially fearful he questions origin and parents. Child says he arose from Gṛtsamada’s sneeze, calls him both father and mother, and asks a few days’ care.
outcome: Actual sneeze-born child confirms origin; no biological human mother assigned.

cause: Newborn ambition motivates initiation and ascetic practice.
details: Newborn promises to conquer three worlds and subdue Indra. Gṛtsamada, fearful and joyful, decides his own Gaṇānāṃ tvā mantra will bring desired boon and his own fame. He initiates child with steady Gaṇeśa-focused practice. Child goes to forest, stands on one toe without food and with controlled senses. After15,000 years (sārdhāyuta), fire from his mouth terrifies gods and lower-world daityas.
outcome: Long mantra practice produces terrifying fire and divine response.

cause: Successful austerity attracts personal divine appearance.
details: Gaṇeśa appears radiant with four arms, axe, lotus, mālā and modakas. Trunk roar/radiance disturb child, who bows and asks a gentler form. Deity draws in brilliance, identifies himself as object of meditation and offers boons, declaring cosmic transcendence. Child thanks him, calls father blessed, says infancy limits praise and asks grant.
outcome: Gentler form makes desired-boon dialogue possible.

cause: Deity offers grant.
details: Child requests power to draw/conquer three worlds; perpetual subjection of gods, dānavas, gandharvas, humans, serpents, rākṣasas, sages, kinnaras and cāraṇas; every mental desire fulfilled; Indra and guardians serving him; earthly enjoyment and final liberation; fame of penance-city as wish-giving Gaṇeśapura.
outcome: Universal domination, desire fulfilment, enjoyment/liberation and site request stated.

cause: Domination request receives detailed grant and exception.
details: Gaṇeśa promises three-world conquest, no fear and all subjects, grants iron/gold/silver three cities, freely moving and unbreakable by gods except Śaṅkara. He names child Tripura. When Śiva breaks his city complex with one arrow, he gains liberation then; all other desires fulfilled by grace. Gaṇeśa vanishes; Tripura grieves separation, rejoices at boons and begins conquest.
outcome: Mobile city boon and one-arrow liberation condition drive forthcoming war.

cause: City boon leads to worship/installation before conquest.
details: After Vyāsa’s question, Tripura installs a Gaṇeśa image of Kashmir stone with mantra-skilled Brahmins, builds a gold jewelled temple at Gaṇeśapura, offers sixteen services, praise/bows, asks leave and gives donations. Gaṇeśapura is situated in Bengal and promises success. He rules human world, recruits the fourfold army from all directions, receives compliant kings’ service and kills opposing rulers.
outcome: Temple established; human sovereignty gained.

cause: Conquest expands from human realm to gods and underworld.
details: Tripura moves on Amarāvatī; armed Indra emerges on Airāvata. Tripura divides his fourfold army into thirds, appoints Bhīmakāya lord of human world and addresses Kālakūṭa/Vajradaṃṣṭra to lead a third to Rasātala and subdue Śeṣa’s Nāgas, taking a third himself against Indra. Bhīmakāya/Vajradaṃṣṭra depart as ordered. Troops break Nandana trees despite resistance. Messengers demand Indra attend Tripura or leave for mortal world where he will be protected; surrender Amarāvatī peacefully or fight.
outcome: Threefold campaign and surrender ultimatum delivered.

cause: Indra rejects surrender and both armies deploy.
details: Indra trembles, ponders then rages and orders messengers to summon battle, roaring from Airāvata. Gods equip swords, bhiṇḍipāla, śakti/ṛṣṭi, clubs, bows/arrows, maces/shields and staffs; Brahmins perform auspicious rites. Tripura emerges mounted on horse with vast army. His huṃkāra sends troops into chaotic mutual slaughter; many on both sides die or lose limbs and vehicle troops fall. Daityas initially flee.
outcome: Mass battle first breaks daitya ranks.

cause: Initial army setback prompts personal counterattack.
details: Tripura checks fleeing troops and personally attacks Indra’s vajra-bearing hand with sword. Fallen vajra he seizes and uses against Airāvata, driving elephant away. Indra punches him down, but risen Tripura punches Indra onto earth.
outcome: Indra disarmed and mount routed; fist exchange begins.

cause: Indra rejects opponent’s refuge offer.
details: Indra demands wrestling. Tripura asks why he risks dear life and offers mortal-world refuge; Indra stakes departure on inability to kill opponent and predicts Tripura’s fall. They strike chest/hands/knees/thighs/heads/elbows/backs/feet, compared with Kṛṣṇa/Cāṇūra. Tripura grabs Indra’s feet, whirls and throws him far out of sight, then mounts four-tusked Airāvata.
outcome: Wrestling ends in Indra’s expulsion; Tripura captures mount.

cause: Indra’s defeat displaces divine rulers.
details: Gods seek Indra in Himalayan caves and find him arriving downcast, embracing/worshipping/fanning/massaging him. They remain secretly there. Tripura enters Amarāvatī on Airāvata, occupies Indra’s throne and assigns divine offices individually to daityas; he enjoys music and service of Gandharvas, Kinnaras and Apsarases.
outcome: Daitya rule installed; gods hide and recover together.

cause: Success over Indra extends to higher abodes.
details: Tripura goes to Brahmā’s abode; forewarned Brahmā withdraws to Viṣṇu’s navel-lotus and Viṣṇu to milk-ocean. Tripura installs mental sons Pracaṇḍa in Brahmaloka and Caṇḍa in Vaikuṇṭha. At Kailāsa his shaking frightens Girijā, who embraces Śiva. Pleased by daitya prowess Śiva offers a boon; Tripura requests Kailāsa and asks Śiva to move to Mandāra as long as his wish lasts. Śiva grants Kailāsa for a short time and departs with attendants.
outcome: Sons occupy two divine realms; brief Kailāsa grant moves Śiva to Mandāra.

cause: Regional commands extend the conquest.
details: Bhīmakāya subdues kings, imprisons sages, destroys sacrificial fire-pits, āśramas and tīrthas, terrorizes ascetics and opposes svāhā/svadhā/vaṣaṭ, Vedic study and good conduct. Vajradaṃṣṭra subdues seven lower worlds including Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and poisonous/nonpoisonous serpents; he enjoys gems/Nāga women, brings treasure and report to Tripura, and receives honour, rich clothes, villages and slaves.
outcome: Ritual support suppressed; underworld treasure and allegiance reported.

cause: Displaced gods seek explanation and remedy.
details: Hidden gods wonder when/by whom Tripura dies and who gave boon. Nārada arrives, receives welcome, hears plea for refuge/remedy and explains a Gaṇeśa boon secured by intense1,000-divine-year austerity as his report here: no fear from gods/sages/ancestors/beings/Yakṣas/Rākṣasas/Piśācas/Nāgas except Śaṅkara. He urges Gaṇeśa worship; asked method, he initiates all in one-syllable mantra and instructs steadfast practice until deity personally gives killing strategy, then departs singing vīṇā.
outcome: Nārada supplies initiation and divine-refuge strategy; duration differs from38 direct scene.

cause: Nārada’s instructions are followed.
details: Gods fast and restrain breath, adopting one-foot, lotus or warrior postures, closed eyes and Gaṇeśa meditation/mantra. After long unspecified time he appears crowned and jeweled, bearing noose, goad, axe and lotus, scented/red/moon-adorned and immensely radiant. Some fear, bow, worship or praise for distress removal.
outcome: Divine appearance enables collective boon request.

cause: Collective dispossession is taken to boon-giver.
details: Gods’ hymn praises supreme causality, cosmic creation/preservation/dissolution, all boons, obstruction removal, knowledge and contrasting devotee/nondevotee outcomes. Deity pleased by hymn+austerity offers boon. They request killing Tripura who seized all offices, citing his own divine protection and taking refuge. He promises removal of all fear; names hymn Saṅkaṭanāśana, granting all wishes to readers/hearers and no distress to three-sandhyā reciters, then vanishes.
outcome: Fear-removal promise and conditional hymn efficacy granted; kill request not yet enacted.

cause: Gaṇeśa’s fear-removal promise prompts disguise strategy.
details: To Vyāsa’s inquiry Brahmā says Gaṇeśa visits Tripura in Brahmin form. Honoured with throne/worship, he identifies himself as Kalādhara, freely wandering all-knowing benefactor, and praises Tripura’s riches beyond divine worlds. Tripura challenges him to demonstrate an extraordinary art, promising desired gift even life and claiming never to speak falsely.
outcome: Demonstration-for-gift bargain accepted.

cause: Art challenge creates occasion for renewed conditional city grant.
details: Kalādhara offers gold/silver/iron three-city complex, wish-giving, freely moving and unbreakable by gods/Gandharvas/humans/serpents, but eventual Śiva single-arrow breach destroys Tripura. Taking bow and fixing arrow, he creates airy cities with buildings/lakes/groves/birds. Māyā deludes Tripura who enters, roars and prides himself unsurpassed.
outcome: Cities actually constructed; recipient deluded into pride.

cause: Demonstrated art activates promised reward.
details: Tripura offers rare gift. Kalādhara requests the extraordinary wish-giving Gaṇeśa image he saw worshipped by Śiva at Kailāsa, promising to spread donor fame. Tripura dismisses Śiva as servant and promises retrieval. He gives ten villages, cattle, clothes/ornaments, pearls/gems/coral, blankets,100 male/female servants, fine horses and silver chariots with gold axles. Kalādhara accepts forced gifts and returns to āśrama, delighting wife/residents as this narrator’s formulation. Nārada reports all events to gods who wait.
outcome: Image retrieval promise brings approaching conflict; gods await strategy.

cause: Image bargain prompts ultimatum.
details: Vyāsa asks about promised image. Tripura sends two messengers to Śiva at Mandāra demanding peaceful delivery of wish-giving Cintāmaṇi image or forced seizure, boasting all rare objects collected. Furious Śiva spares them because they are envoys, saying otherwise they would burn like Kāma; challenges Tripura to battle and says image cannot be won even after100 births. Envoys report refusal.
outcome: Envoy immunity preserves messengers; refusal makes war inevitable.

cause: Śiva rejects image seizure.
details: Enraged Tripura sends vast fourfold army to Mandāra and follows mounted on mind-speed aerial city complex, adorned in jewel-armour, earrings/crown/ornaments, with powerful bow, quiver, tortoise-type shield, sword and divine śakti. Gandharvas/Apsarases, bards and Cāraṇas precede him. Śiva hears approach, explicitly worships, bows and circumambulates Gaṇeśa in this passage, then marches with troops and trident.
outcome: Two armies deploy;42 worship statement retained despite later contrary explanation.

cause: Deployments meet in general combat.
details: Noisy armies clash in dust and lose friend/enemy distinction. When dust settles, individual duels use prāsa, swords, sharpened arrows, ṛṣṭi, fists, axes, tomara and trees. Slaughter of foot/horse/chariot/elephant troops makes a river of blood. Śiva and city-mounted Tripura draw near while gods/daityas arrange individual duels whose names Brahmā promises next.
outcome: Mass battle becomes distinct named duels.

cause: Leaders meet and retinues duel.
details: Brahmā enumerates duels: Ṣaṇmukha vs Pracaṇḍa; Nandin vs Caṇḍa; Puṣpadanta vs Bhīmakāya; Bhṛśuṇḍī vs Kālakūṭa; Vīrabhadra vs Vajradaṃṣṭra; Indra vs unnamed daitya minister; Jayanta vs unnamed daitya son; gods’ teacher vs Kāvya. Vehicle peers fight peers and some abandon weapons for wrestling.
outcome: All named pairings recorded; no unsupported outcome for Kāvya duel.

cause: Named duels proceed through arrow-counterarrow exchanges.
details: Pracaṇḍa fires nine arrows; Kārttikeya cuts them before arrival and strikes with five, making Pracaṇḍa faint/fall. Nandin’s five sharpened arrows similarly drop Caṇḍa. Bhīmakāya shoots ten at Puṣpadanta who cuts all, hits with three and drops him. Bhṛśuṇḍī drops Kālakūṭa with five arrows.
outcome: Four daitya opponents incapacitated; deaths not asserted when fall/faint is stated.

cause: Individual counterattacks defeat daitya champions.
details: Vīrabhadra fires four at Vajradaṃṣṭra, who blocks and replies with three. Vīrabhadra cuts those with three then drops opponent with three. Indra drops daitya minister with vajra. Unnamed son advances with sword on Jayanta; Jayanta cuts sword with arrow and hits with three, causing blood-vomit and unconscious fall. Daityas flee and victorious Pramathas pursue.
outcome: Initial divine victory breaks enemy troops.

cause: Tripura intervenes after retinue defeats.
details: Tripura personally approaches Śiva in his cities, moves from physical weapons to astras, and releases Vāruṇa weapon: torrential rain/mist and lightning obscure battlefield and stonefall/wind rout Śiva’s army. Śiva releases Vāyavya, breaking clouds, whirling daitya troops, stripping hats/feathers, crushing vehicles and uprooting vegetation. Tripura counters wind with Pannaga weapon.
outcome: Rain→wind→serpent sequence changes battlefield advantage.

cause: Countered wind is followed by fire weapon and persistent combatant.
details: Tripura shoots Anala-enchanted arrow causing coal-rain and flames. From flames arises huge hunger-driven fanged roaring man, tongue100yojanas, nose-wind hurling elephants, who devours Śiva’s troops. They beg Śiva’s protection. He reassures, suppresses fire with Parjanya astra and drops man with one arrow, but man rises and resumes eating. Pramathas flee stumbling/shaking; unsupported Śiva retreats into cave.
outcome: Rain suppresses fire but arrow fails to stop revived man; Śiva retreats.

cause: Divine retreat exposes Girijā to capture attempt.
details: Ṣaḍānana and other heroes follow retreating Śiva. Tripura seeks to seize solitary Girijā at Kailāsa; she sees approach, goes to father and asks protection. Father hides her in inaccessible secret cave. Tripura comes to Himalayan mountain but cannot find her; sees Cintāmaṇi image, seizes it and returns victorious toward lower world. Image vanishes in his hand; he takes this as ominous, re-enters city distressed.
outcome: Girijā protected; stolen image vanishes, denying promised transfer.

cause: Retreat prompts reflection and adviser arrival.
details: Vyāsa asks defeat remedy. Śiva worries about earth deprived of svāhā/svadhā and gods’ restoration, welcomes Nārada and reports routed gods in unknown locations and thousands of countered astras. Nārada reverently acknowledges all-knowledge/power, reflects and offers requested advice.
outcome: Śiva solicits a remedy, acknowledging battlefield failure.

cause: Nārada gives omission-of-worship explanation and exact boon counter.
details: Nārada says Śiva failed to worship Gaṇeśa before battle and must now propitiate him, get boon and win. He recalls Tripura’s immunity except Maheśvara and prescribes one arrow to split three mobile cities. Śiva agrees and remembers earlier one-/six-syllable initiation, saying battle preoccupation caused no recitation/remembrance. Nārada again urges worship; Śiva leaves for austerity.
outcome: Śiva accepts remembrance/initiation remedy; source discrepancy retained.

cause: Accepted advice leads to renewed ascetic japa.
details: In Daṇḍakāraṇya Śiva sits lotus-postured with restrained senses and focused japa/meditation, practicing100years. A five-faced ten-armed figure with moon brow, skull garland, serpent adornments, crown/armlets and ten unspecified weapons emerges from his mouth, radiant beyond sun/fire/moon. Śiva wonders whether doubled himself, disguised Tripura, dream, or Gaṇeśa. Figure identifies as inwardly contemplated obstacle-remover, cosmic lord pleased with austerity and invites all desired boons.
outcome: Personal appearance and boon invitation after100years.

cause: Boon invitation prompts praise/name explanation.
details: Asked by a sage/Brahmā’s narrative framing what Śiva requested, Śiva praises his ten eyes/arms and five heads/faces as fulfilled by vision/worship, then Gaṇeśa as origin of elements/senses/gods/sages/ancestors/Viṣṇu-Brahmā-Śiva and cosmic functions. Brahmā’s first-person speech says he spoke at Śiva’s command, deriving Gaṇeśa name from lordship of gaṇas and Oṃ as primary letter-seed; deity assents.
outcome: Name derivation and assent precede grace request; first-person switch preserved.

cause: Śiva acknowledges omission and asks forgiveness/victory.
details: Śiva grants Gaṇeśa-related remembrance/worship efficacy: remembering at tasks gives obstacle-free completion; Gaṇeśa is to be worshipped first in Śaiva/Gāṇapatya/Vaiṣṇava/Śākta/Saura and Vedic/worldly auspicious/inauspicious activities.45.10 lacks secure negative in without-remembrance clause and is not emended. Śiva says neglected worship/bows/remembrance caused defeat and requests forgiveness and victory at battles. He expresses that nondevotees become dull/poor and devotees gain wish-granting success.
outcome: First-worship efficacy spoken; personal request stated with textual uncertainty.

cause: Forgiveness/victory request receives practical boon strategy.
details: Gaṇeśa promises Śiva his arrival whenever remembered, and instructs enchanting one arrow with deity’s name-seed to bring down three cities by his radiance and reduce daitya to ash. He teaches thousand names granting victory/wishes; war-time recitation kills daityas swiftly, three-sandhyā recitation fulfils all desired wishes.
outcome: Remembered appearance, seed-arrow and war hymn prescribed; actual destruction still future.

cause: Personal grant prompts installation and hopeful report.
details: Śiva worships rejoicing, installs Mahāgaṇeśa and builds a high strong temple, satisfies gods/sages/Siddhas and gives Brahmin gifts, worships/bows again and proclaims city Maṇipūra. Gaṇeśa and assembled gods/sages vanish. Śiva returns with attendants, Gandharvas/Yakṣas/divine women and tells Girijā; gods/sages with spouses rejoice, treating Tripura as already dead and their offices regained in anticipation.
outcome: Actual temple established; enemy death/office restoration only anticipated at this point.

cause: Booned war hymn receives explicit ritual frame.
details: Vyāsa requests the taught thousand names. Brahmā repeats neglected worship/obstacles and subsequent proper Mahāgaṇapati worship before instruction. Ritual heading names Gaṇeśa as ṛṣi, Mahāgaṇapati/Śvānandeśa Brahmaṇaspati as deity, varied metres, gaṃ seed, tuṇḍa śakti and svāhā key; ritual aim all-obstacle destruction and divine pleasure. Limb/heart nyāsas precede red three-eyed elephant deity meditation with noose, goad, axe and reassurance, joined by Śakti, Siddhi/Buddhi. Invocation also names Lakṣa/Lābha and family/vehicle/weapon/enclosure setting, then five mental services.
outcome: Formula and meditation documented; heading alternate readings retained.

cause: Thousand-name teaching prescribed for war.
details: Gaṇeśa speaks a dense thousand-name hymn. Names praise forms, weapons/mounts, cosmic body, abilities, ritual seats/śaktis, mantras, script-letter sequence, traditions and numerical series. Origin/family epithets include Umāputra, Īśānaputra, Śambhu-mouth/emotion emergence, Umā-body/Gaurī-radiance/Gaṅgā emergence, Kaśyapasuta and Ṣaṇmukha-bhrātā; these are hymn epithets rather than separate enacted birth stories. Whole verse body read; individual name segmentation and every embedded kinship/śakti/weapon implication remain unextracted and prevent chapter COMPLETE.
outcome: Hymn read; atomic segmentation/claim checking deliberately pending.

details: Daily Brahma-muhūrta recitation promises all worldly/otherworldly happiness. Single japa also promises longevity, health, sovereignty, courage, valour, strength, fame, intelligence/discernment, firmness, beauty/good fortune, truth, mercy, forgiveness, peace, generosity, righteousness, world-control/dialogue skill/debate eloquence, public learning, depth, brahmic radiance, high lineage/conduct/power/nobility, knowledge/discriminative knowledge/faith and wealth/grain increase.
outcome: General material/ethical/intellectual efficacy attached to timed daily or single recitation.

details: Japa promises subjection of king, royal wife, royal son and minister, with targeted subject becoming servant; easy four-goal attainment; protection from Śākinī/Ḍākinī/Rākṣasa/Yakṣa/serpent fear; imperial happiness/enemy defeat; discord removal, burned-seed sprouting, bad-dream relief and angry-master appeasement; six rites/eight major siddhis/three-time knowledge; hostile ritual/army suppression; battle victory; infertility-removal/pregnancy protection. Daily recitation in a region prevents famine/calamity/evil.
outcome: Targeted domination, protections, battle/ritual powers and regional outcomes stated.

details: Wealth does not leave a home where hymn is recited. Single japa calms listed illnesses: wasting, leprosy, urinary disorders, piles, fistula, viṣūcikā, abdominal masses/spleen/stone/diarrhoea/enlarged belly, cough/breath distress/udāvarta/pain/swelling, head disease/vomiting/hiccups/gland swelling/no appetite, vāta-pitta-kapha mixed/tridoṣa fevers, externally caused/irregular/cold/hot/one-day and other fevers, and named/unnamed disease faults. Women, Śūdras and fallen persons also attain success through single reading; parenthetical193 reading retained.
outcome: Specific religious cure/prosperity efficacy and inclusive beneficiary statement documented.

details: Desire-driven reciter enjoys earthly wishes and pleasant aerial vehicles/divine wish fruits, moves in desired forms/directions among Moon/Indra/Sun/Upendra/Brahmā/Rudra abodes, enjoys with chosen kin, becomes beloved Mahāgaṇapati attendant welcomed by Nandīśvara/gaṇas and cherished as son by Śiva couple; through Gaṇeśa boon becomes righteous universal sovereign remembering past lives.
outcome: Desire-driven enjoyment, divine service and remembered-birth kingship promised in order.

details: Desireless constant devoted reciter attains supreme yoga, knowledge/dispassion and blissful Vaināyaka abode without return. Thousand-name worship subdues kings/enemies and perfects all mantras/siddhis. Hymn called dearer than root mantra. At deity’s birth on bright fourth of Nabhas month, devotional dūrvā/name worship, prescribed libation and eight-substance homa accomplish all wishes. Recitation/reading/teaching/hearing/exposition/discussion/meditation/review/approval yield full prosperity here and beyond.
outcome: Desireless liberation distinguished from desired enjoyment; ritual occasion and varied reception efficacy registered.

details: One who carries hymn even wandering freely is guarded by eight crores of Śiva-born gaṇas. Written hymn worship brings constant highest Lakṣmī; name remembrance exceeds collective donations/vows/tīrthas/sacrifices. Daily sunrise/noon/evening/three-bathing-time/constant reading brings eloquence/fame, wealth, obstacle removal, control and descendants. Poor one-pointed restrained eater practicing Gaṇeśa worship+japa four months uproots poverty accompanying seven births and gains great wealth; daily reciters gain disease-free life, pure lineage, generous wealth, fame, fresh speech/beauty, good sons and virtuous desired spouse.
outcome: Protection, written-hymn worship, timed recitation and four-month poverty remedy conditions stated.

details: Twenty-one names beginning Gaṇañjaya/Gaṇapati/Heramba/Dharaṇīdhara and ending Kāśyapa/Nandana/Vācāsiddha/Ḍhuṇḍhi/Vināyaka accompany devoted modaka offering for a year for desired success. Deity treats fixed-mind worshipful praise as thousand-name praise. Closing salutations and names beseech crossing the ocean of becoming and removal of evil. Individual name inventory remains pending, with duplicate217/219 numbering preserved.
outcome: Year-long abbreviated offering efficacy closes whole read hymn.

cause: Victory boon/mantra renew divine morale.
details: After boon/thousand names Śiva joyfully dances/roars and summons troops/gods for renewed battle. Brahmā, Kubera, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, Soma, Varuṇa and Aryamā, with Gandharvas/Yakṣas/planets/Kinnaras, bow and praise, asking when displaced gods will see enemy killed. Śiva marches gladly, inwardly contemplating Gaṇeśa, to enemy abode.
outcome: Second campaign begins with explicit inward remembrance.

cause: Spies announce renewed assault and enemy mobilizes.
details: Spies report Śiva’s return; Tripura equips army with astras/weapons/armour, rewards fighters with cloth/garlands/ornaments/wealth, and mounts city complex. Armies clash with varied weapons and vital-piercing iron arrows, capture/kill, seize hair and behead, raising dust darkness and blood rivers. Wind clears dust, revealing dead gods, fleeing divine troops and rejoicing daityas.
outcome: Second battle initially breaks god army.

cause: Indra’s counterattack again provokes Tripura intervention.
details: Vajra-bearing Indra enters, frightening daityas and crushing/killing/mutilating troops with vajra. Tripura challenges him to leave alive, promises not to strike his back, compares contest to goat/lion, then showers arrows. One enchanted arrow produces countless missiles covering sky/earth, blinding/mutilating gods/Gandharvas. Indra falls under blows, gods faint; Śiva inwardly admires Tripura’s prowess despite raging battle.
outcome: Multiplying arrow overwhelms gods and drops Indra; Śiva assesses opponent.

cause: Battlefield defeat prompts last reminder of exact exception.
details: Nārada arrives and advises Śiva not to worry, recalling difficult Gaṇeśa austerity, comprehensive boon and city complex unbreakable by gods with one-arrow breach exception leading to death. After his departure Śiva revives/alerts unconscious gods, remembers elephant-faced deity’s instruction recalled by adviser, and prepares deliberate killing strategy.
outcome: Gods restored to alertness; Śiva recalls divine command and acts.

cause: Exact boon exception is prepared through cosmic weapon assembly/mantra.
details: Śiva constructs cosmic chariot: moon/sun wheels, mountain bow, Acyuta/Viṣṇu arrow and Aśvin pair as draft horses. Printed kurūpaṃ chariot-material and yaṃtāram indīvarajaṃ driver clause remain pending exact collation; conventional Earth/Brahmā reconstruction is not silently asserted. After ācamana/inward deity contemplation he recites thousand names with one-syllable mantra, enchants fierce Pināka and Viṣṇu-form great arrow. Earth, Śeṣa, forests/mountains and celestial bodies quake/whirl; bow sound confuses gods/humans.
outcome: Enchanted single arrow readied; two chariot lexical details unresolved.

cause: Name/mantra-enchanted single arrow realizes boon’s exception.
details: Śiva releases great arrow, flames fill sky/earth/lower worlds. Tripura with army flees in cities, but swift arrow burns daitya and three cities. Daitya’s bodily radiance merges into Śiva while armies watch. Heavenly voice announces Śiva-slain daitya liberated. Gods/sages praise the three-eyed victor.
outcome: Actual destruction, divine merging and liberation explicitly narrated.

cause: Liberation/death ends domination and ritual suppression.
details: Gandharvas/Cāraṇas sing, Apsarases dance, Kinnaras play music and Nārada’s divine sages shower flowers. Śiva sends gods back to their offices; sages resume fear-free Veda/Vedāṅga practice and people renew agnihotra/sacrifices/donations/vows. Attendants including Śailādi, Gaṇapa and Skanda bow; Śiva dismantles/divides great chariot and returns decorated Kailāsa amid victory music. Tripurāri name spreads; narrator identifies mantra/thousand-name power and promises all wishes for reading/hearing account.
outcome: Divine offices and social ritual restored; Śiva returns, closing warfare with lexical chariot/hymn atomic gaps separately pending.

cause: Completed destruction prompts dating/festival aftermath question.
details: Vyāsa acknowledges Tripura-killing account and asks where Jagadambā remained, her return and date/place of burning. Brahmā dates destruction to evening full moon called Bāhulā after daytime war, explaining lamp-gifts and multiplied bath/donation/japa/homa efficacy. Nonobservance of Tripurāri festival forfeits victory/burns merit; morning Śiva worship erases night’s sins, noon worship lifetime sins, evening worship seven-birth sins.48.9 begins separate Girijā-emergence/reunion account.
outcome: Full-moon evening endpoint and differentiated ritual efficacy supplied; ensuing Girijā return/worship instruction continues48.9–50.33 in gup3.

details: Seventh-year daily rites, lion and four weapons/ascetic ornaments; playful cosmic roar delights parents.

King receives hospitality and requests purohita for son’s wedding; Cāturmāsya prevents Kaśyapa travelling. Son substituted, bows parents, boards chariot; Aditi requires constant care and safe return, king agrees.
Narrative flashback identifies paternal uncle/brother,10000-year inverted smoky Sun tapas, weapon and dominion request. Sun sends unfailing radiant weapon; dominion not explicitly granted.
Child flies, intercepts weapon and tosses to test power; fall splits Dhūmrākṣa, fragments crush surrounding rocks/trees500bow-lengths. King wonders at destiny.
Sons accuse king of killing their father/protector. Afraid of Narāntaka king asserts wedding purpose and offers child. Child protests breach of parental trust and warns Kaśyapa’s anger.
Roar/breath launches attacking sons; after two muhūrtas they fall into Narāntaka city crushing homes. Messengers discover both alive and transmit their report.
1000rākṣasas ordered to capture child/kill if fighting. Roar kills some; others injured, including arrow-torn bellies, flee and report.
Survivors warn child unbeatable; Narāntaka ridicules warning, equips host and orders plunder/distraction or killing king and child. Commander threatens any disobedient demon.
City reception and sixteen-offering worship; eager women seek sight, one barred woman dies while meditating. Four social groups perceive varied forms according to disposition.
Child knowingly counters malicious play-embrace by crushing both demons; ten-yojana corpses and divine flower/praise follow.
Whirlwinds devastate city and lift chariot; child immobilizes chariot, grabs topknots, whirls and kills both. King bows recognizing divine creator and countless forms.
Axe splits disguised stone100ways; child fists emerging terrifying demon down after onlookers flee.
King seats, worships, feeds child/friends and prepares night bed after sandhyā; four guards stationed while king/queen retire by child’s leave.
After morning rites child plays. Kaśyapa’s friend Dharmadatta invites incarnate Lord to purify household; child willingly follows.
Two sent demons fall toward child as fighting donkeys; child grabs feet, whirls/smashes both dead. Direct sight confirms fame for Dharmadatta.
Rampaging disguised elephant fights royal animals amid destruction. Child refuses shelter, mounts and goads temples to death; falling body crushes homes. Rescued from corpse, carried indoors.
Devotee worships/feeds and gives Siddhi/Buddhi as dakṣiṇā, praises divine visit lifting ancestry; child seats/honors him and appears with both.
Dhūmrākṣa’s wife feigns kindly massage, applies poison, causes burning. Child knows evil, strikes head with coconut, exposing two-yojana corpse.
Renewed meal/worship and divine celebrations; king brings child home in musical procession. Lion/weapon appearance and paired attendants celebrated; hearing benefit concludes.

King recounts victories with retrospective names Kūṭa/Kuṇḍa and proposes wedding preparations. Two ministers blame continued child presence for dangers; wedding postponed fortnight/month with agreement.
Revenge trio plans fire, wind and devouring. Vast tiger-maw and mouth-fire destroy city; refugees swallowed, mistaking mouth for cave. Source fire attribution retained with textual caution.

King protects entrusted child while abandoning belongings/family, regrets but recalls duty and earlier rescues. Fort/water defense fails against wind-fire; armies/citizens flee, king/child lose and search one another.

Child enters closed tiger-maw, expands/splits demon dead. One half cast away, other playhouse; captives arise. Drinks fire, footstroke crushes final attackers (Vidāraṇa wording), yogamāyā revives all dead/restores city.
People/king praise rescue and resurrection. Healthy homecomings/daily rites, gifts/peace-worship/redistribution and rest conclude; devotional hearing yields desires/no disasters.

King’s meal invitation reveals child already fed/adorned by remote bright-fourth worship. Child identifies sage, ascetic trunk/ressemblance, temporal knowledge and cosmic power; three deities seek sight.
Vināyaka dictates first invitation/name. King travels armed horseback, honors sage/hermitage, gives wedding invitation; identifies Sun-lineage self and Kaśyapa’s child.
Sage asks deity form; king describes divine four-arm birth then ordinary seventh-year Brahmacārin. Sage refuses since not own meditation-deity, while offering obedience if own Lord calls.
King accepts cannot compel. Sage compassionately hand-blesses and returns closed-eyed king instantly home; king reports happiness/sorrow and warns coercing brāhmaṇas brings ashes.
After exact report child laughs, supplies name Gajānana and instantly sends king back. Sage ecstatic on name, sets out; Earth trembles, reassured, and third step reaches Kāśī.

Sage threatens curse, refuses two-arm child as lesser. Describes own ten-arm peacock form; child adopts exact lotus-seated form. Sage loves/dances/worships, Lord embraces ten-armed, king worships both.
Lord explains forms responsive to devotion and earth/Brahmā/Aditi incarnation cause; promises demon destruction, god restoration and departure after brothers killed, as future purpose.
Sage requests repeated direct sight of exact form and Āśāpūraka name’s fame. Lord grants both and adds all wishes fulfilled/constant remembrance. Child plays; sage meditates.
Witnesses marvel, king praises rare sight, feeds/beds child and retires with permission.
Next-day frame; demon’s ornate brāhmaṇa astrologer guise and claimed three-time/peace expertise. King asks identity/causes before lodging/upkeep.
Visitor urges abandon child, predicts flood/mountain and royal overthrow. King distrusts, cites child divine powers/rescues, refuses harmful intent and challenges visitor take child himself.
Hand inspection predicts four-day well/sea/darkness/mountain/twoDeath dangers, offers four-day removal with oath. Child goes indoors for countertest.
Child’s stolen-ring challenge gains visitor identification and desired reward, then consecrated ring pierces demon heart. Corpse damages city; divine celebration, worship/gifts and play follow.
Gifted revenge pair with Brahmā-boon descriptor dismisses fourfold host, plans well/frog+child lure. King admires magically appearing well; Kandara invites play.
Child pushed into deep water, feigns drowning by māyā and pulls demon under. Crowds fear death, king offers any reward/own life; three rescuers submerged by demon illusion; parental-duty lament.
Child pushes Kandara into frog mouth; mistaken swallowing provokes belly-tearing then neck-biting, demons kill each other. Bodies removed, magical well closed, child plays.
People moralize deceptive self-destruction/unassailable child, king gifts and dismisses, gods celebrate; narrator marks unfathomable māyā/destiny/incarnation.
Wedding delayed by successive dangers. Terrifying trio plans fire/darkness/flood/flying-mountain blockade; roars disturb worlds/seas and Andhaka covers Sun.
Sudden night interrupts rituals/trades, populace guesses causes and lights lamps; demon-cloud rain, lightning/storm/flood destroy homes with deaths.

Child’s māyā creates100-yojana tree and giant bird, lights city/drinks water, wings shelter all people/animals while enduring fiery/hail rain. Eleven days ordinary work resumes; simultaneous playing child hides identity.

Exhausted two await Tuṅga’s5-yojana mountain. Bird catches mountain in beak, others one each foot, circles above Bhuvar; fatigue/Sun heat killallthree. Corpses fall/crush woods; banyan/illusion and bird form disappear.
King embraces, people ask welfare/worship/praise, Sun/rivers/restored conditions return. Flowers/music/city entry/gifts/peace-homa/cattle distribution and meal conclude.

Head returns, grieving kin swoons/lament praises strength and twin consecration; friends counsel scouts/cremation/tears restraint. Demoness chooses head-in-oil preservation and revenge with Aditi-son head.
Beautiful Aditi guise deceives royal welcome; false mother demands child, king reassures safety/praises rescues and promises return both after wedding, yet she insists separation grief.
Knowing deception child eats poisoned laddu and demands more; heavybody prevents fauxmother rising. She/bystanders plead and fail to lift sleeping child; demoness dies, ten-yojana form revealed.
Child lifted flower-light after death. People praise cognition/cosmic sovereignty/forms/devotional liberation; corpse cut and discarded outside, homecomings follow.
Three-junction hymn recitation prevents calamity/obstacle/spiritfear, fulfills wishes and gains continuous protection.

Citizens request shared home visits; king urges genuine worship not testing, child challenges ordinary-boy benefits and many houses. Leaders insist before postwedding departure; child consents subject royal permission.

Poor learned restrained household prepares modest worship; wife doubts luxury bypass, husband insists devotion matters. Eighteen-grain bread/watery oldrice, simple aromatic/forest/bark offerings and yard rites prepared.

Child bathes/visits loving poorcouple, accepts kuśa/footwater/dūrvā/śamī worship and ashamed coarse meal. Declares devotional food exceeds nectar; ten arms manage watery rice. Sharers godlike, mockers regret; āmalaka mouth-cleaning.

Invited boon: Śukla asks stable devotion and final no-return liberation, already fulfilled by sight. Lord assents and adds superior gem-goldhouse, beauty/knowledge/wealth; resumes twoarms, departs with leave.
King honors sages seeking divine sight. Seeing modaka-bearing child in royal house they reject impurity; child challenges lost knowledge. Refuse royal meal and depart bathing.
Prepared households seek departed child, find him returned sleeping and protest poorhouse choice. Child full, ostentatious eat own food; true devotees fast/meditate.
Lord manifests in all faithful houses, sleeps/recites/gives/teaches/eats. Each enjoys bath/worship/feast believing first host; king wonders simultaneous palace presence and vehicles.

Hungry sages find Vināyaka in all mundane/devotional activities and Śukla house, flee leftovers but every direction/thing/heart meditation is Lord. See lion tenarm cosmicform, abandon distinctions and bow, awakened by grace.

Hymn acknowledges confusion and cosmiccause. Lord grants truthknowledge/omniscience, vanishes. Pair builds Varada image/temple and tank, states bath-worship benefits through final abode, gods worship and sages depart.

King/people honor shrine/brāhmaṇas. Vyāsa asks Śukla’s extraordinary unrequested rewards; Brahmā explains devoted feeling/simple offerings vs ostentation, introduces hunter’s śamī-leaf sālokya for next chapter.
Vyāsa asks hunter example. Cruel meat-seller Bhīma hunts festival sale/familyfood, pursued by devouring Piṅgākṣa, drops weapons and climbs śamī tree; demon follows, branch thrown.
Wind carries leaf onto Vāmana-established deity image, Lord accepts pair as worshippers. Vāmana boon-appearance and dūrvā/śamī devotion teaching interposed; divine vehicle sent.
Sight of Lord-shaped messengers/grace destroys sins; pair receive divine bodies, honored/transported and bow; attain sārūpya in ownrealm till kalpa end.
Śukla’s smallmeal/Alakā-like house compares devotional power; leaves/devotion valued over show. Pastlife/origin questions continue outside bounded arc27.

Śaunaka asks location and manifestation date. Sūta places Vakratunda at the eastern limit, installed by gods/sages/Gaṇas, manifest on Bhādra bright fourth; midday worship gives immense siddhis, beginning/end less. Images lie in each island/region’s east; square field ten yojanas, deity central with Siddhi left/Buddhi right, lion in front, eight siddhis in eight directions, eight Gaṇas and Śiva/Viṣṇu/Sun/Śakti in four directions.

Brahmā and deities occupy east/behind, Gaṅgā and rivers south, Kāśī and fields west, Vasiṣṭha and sages north. Śeṣa/Nāga kings, Gandharvas, mountains, Siddhas, Apsarases, Vidyādharas and Kinnaras serve joyfully and exchange Vakratunda stories; bathing in the ocean they create tīrthas bearing their names.

Gaṇeśa tīrtha bathing fulfils life; pilgrimage gives desired ends; dying in the field gives Brahman state. Distant remembrance gives enduring liberation by śukla-gati; devotees anywhere attain Brahman and purify people by sight. Sūta limits his account: even Śeṣa, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Vedas, Skanda and yogins cannot exhaust it, and he repeats Mudgala’s account to Dakṣa.

Śaunaka asks what followed Mudgala’s discourse to Dakṣa. Dakṣa asks the detailed Dhundhirāja incarnation and how Vakratunda is born from Śaṅkara’s body. Mudgala introduces an old Gaṇeśa account Yājñavalkya taught Kauśika, illuminating Brahminhood.

Bhārgava sage Ṛcīka grows old through long austerity, sees deer with mates/descendants, desires household life and asks king Gādhi’s daughter. Gādhi demands a thousand dark-eared horses as his established marriage-price. Ṛcīka gets them from Varuṇa and gives them; frightened Gādhi duly marries his daughter to him. Her mother laments, provides goods/clothes and sends her to the forest, where she diligently serves Ṛcīka.

Pleased by his wife’s good conduct, Ṛcīka uses his own austerity to create a richly adorned forest city with four social classes, servants and wealth, and adopts a youthful form. He enjoys marriage properly, then judges its pleasures small and becomes unattached.

The queen visits with wealth/clothes and finds a magnificent city rather than the hermitage; a sweeper identifies Ṛcīka’s city and summons her daughter. Seeing the prosperous sage, she tells her daughter to ask him for sons for both women. Ṛcīka prepares two carus/puroḍāśas with Brahmin/Kṣatriya potency and specifies each eater, then leaves for midday rites. The mother orders exchanging their portions; daughter complies, mother returns home, both become pregnant.

Ṛcīka sees fierce radiance in his wife and asks about Kṣatriya potency. She admits the exchange; he predicts her brother will be an ascetic, her son a fierce bowman. Afraid, she asks a Brahmin son and threatens her life otherwise. He shifts that quality to her grandson, informs Viṣṇu of the pregnancy and effects it through tapas. Jamadagni is born to him; Rāma, best bearer of weapons, becomes Jamadagni’s son. Gādhi’s queen bears Viśvāmitra in ninth month; Gādhi installs his grown son in the kingdom and leaves for austerity.

King Viśvāmitra hunts, grows hungry/thirsty and reaches Vasiṣṭha’s hermitage. Vasiṣṭha feeds king and army by the cow’s power. Viśvāmitra requests Nandinī; refused, he orders her seizure. She destroys the messengers; when men whip her, she creates a great army which destroys the king’s whole army. He returns defeated.

Viśvāmitra leaves rule to ministers and propitiates Śaṅkara in forest. At100 years Śiva grants complete missile knowledge. He returns, attacks Vasiṣṭha and hermitage with fire missile and other weapons. Vasiṣṭha’s Brahmadaṇḍa destroys every missile and defeats him; he flees. Brahmins comfort Vasiṣṭha. Viśvāmitra recognizes Brahmin power’s superiority and his destroyed weapons.

Viśvāmitra abandons kingdom, fasts and repeats Gāyatrī by puraścaraṇa for Brahminhood, scorching the world. At10,000 years Brahmā offers a boon; his Brahminhood request is answered with further austerity. Brahmā comes ten times offering another boon, which he refuses. His tapas subjects gods and awes Brahmins into assent to his claimed Brahmarṣi rank; Vasiṣṭha still calls him Rājarṣi. Furious, he repeatedly attempts Vasiṣṭha’s death without success and remains distressed.

Yājñavalkya, explicitly arisen from Brahmā’s limb, visits. Viśvāmitra bows, worships and says birth, study and austerity bear fruit through seeing him; he asks the visit’s purpose and offers obedience as his servant.

Yājñavalkya came only because he knew Viśvāmitra’s grief, promises to remove it by reasoned knowledge, and hears the denied boon and Vasiṣṭha’s Rājarṣi address. He promises Brahmarṣi rank after relinquishing pride/envy and offers the Kāśī–Viśveśvara story: their inseparability even at dissolution produces pride and a separating obstacle. Viśvāmitra asks its nature.

After60 rainless years and terrestrial devastation, Brahmā approaches Sūrya-line king Divodāsa, who left rule and performs devotional tapas for liberation. Brahmā asks him to take Kāśī to save life, promising rainfall if he rules. He first refuses, asking liberation; then compassionately accepts on condition earthly rule excludes gods, while gods/heaven, humans/earth and Nāgas/Rākṣasas/Pātāla keep their domains. He will worship Śambhu as a deity; Brahmā agrees and grants Kāśī.

Brahmā takes Śiva with gods/sages to Mandara to grant Marīci a boon, warning the ascetic will die otherwise. Marīci asks liberation; suffering from tapas he relinquishes life, obtains Śiva’s likeness and reaches Kailāsa. Brahmā then asks Śiva to remain at Mandara, explaining Divodāsa’s condition for drought relief and asking pardon. Śiva agrees with a sigh and stays with Pārvatī/Gaṇas.

Śiva laments that Avimukta was taken from him and his Viśvanātha title is powerless. Recognizing obstacle and removal of pride, he resolves refuge in Vighnarāja and meditates on Gaṇeśa at the mountain for Kāśī. Personified Kāśī hears his departure, loses pride and meditates on Vighneśa for Śiva. Divodāsa’s righteous reign restores rain, joy and sinless observance of social duties.

Healthy people, fruitful trees, abundant cow milk, sacrifices and svāhā/svadhā please gods/ancestors. Divodāsa’s daily circuit worships Dhundhi first, then Viśveśvara, Jagadambā, Kāśī, Maṇikarṇī, Bhāgīrathī, Mādhava, Jaigīṣavya cave, Kālabhairava and Daṇḍapāṇi. He makes people perform this and punishes the unrighteous;80,000 years pass without even slight sin entering.

Gods resent loss of earthly sovereignty and scheme against the king. Indra orders Agni to withdraw outward fire; people seek Divodāsa, who assumes fire-form by tapas everywhere on earth. As other gods withdraw he supplies their functions through forms including Vāyu, unknown to the people. Gods ask Brahmā what to do; he sends them to request restored places. They praise Divodāsa, he praises them and restores their offices, remaining in one human body. Agni and others resume their places. The transcription misnumbers sequential63 as33.

Śiva grieves that the righteous tapas-powered king cannot be displaced. Gods/sages offer to lure citizens by siddhis so their sin falls on king, then Śiva can take Kāśī. Their many forms and siddhis fail for a year because citizens remain righteous. Śiva’s further dispatched Bhairavas, Ādityas, Vasus, sages, Yoginīs and Gaṇas fail. Brahmā is sent and performs ten Aśvamedhas, then becomes quiet.

Śiva meditates on Vighnarāja for one year, asking freedom from obstacles and separation. Seeing complete humility, Vakratunda manifests lion-mounted, four-armed, noose/goad/boon/fearlessness, red elephant face, great belly, Siddhi/Buddhi, Śeṣa at navel and Cintāmaṇi. Śiva worships/hymns creator/preserver/destroyer and causal/transcendent forms, seeks inseparable Kāśī, and recalls an earlier promise to appear in son-relation on remembrance. Vakratunda promises hymn recitation/hearing gives siddhis, enjoyment/liberation and all other requests, restoring Avimukta meaning.

Vakratunda creates a beautiful all-knowing radiant Brahmin from his body and directs him to delude Kāśī citizens and Divodāsa and restore rule to Śiva. People will call him Dhundhi the astrologer and honor him, his descendants likewise. The Brahmin bows, circles and goes remembering Gaṇeśa. Vakratunda commands Viṣṇu to enter Kāśī in Buddhist form and corrupt the already-deluded city. Viṣṇu obeys; both accomplish the ordered delusion and corruption.

Kāśī meditates for a thousand years; lion-mounted adorned Gaṇeśa arrives. She rises, bows, worships and hymns infinite/formless/formful, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, protector and obstacle-giver to nondevotees. Afflicted separation makes her Avimukta name empty; she asks Śiva’s sight. He promises return, meaningful Avimukta name, hymn that removes separation, desired ends and Brahman state to faithful reciters/hearers. He disappears; she keeps meditating, awaiting the time.

Dhundhi astrologer instantly deludes the city; Viṣṇu as Buddha then corrupts it. Divodāsa is instructed by Dhundhi and gives up rule through the Buddhist figure, awaiting Śiva. Both summon Śiva, who leads worshipped Gaṇeśa into Kāśī as first resident, then enters with gods/sages. Kāśī bows to both; gods/sages take places and Śiva grants Divodāsa liberation.

Gaṇeśa tells Śiva he restored Kāśī and will return to his own abode, visible again on Śiva’s remembrance; he disappears with Dhundhi Brahmin. Śiva creates and installs his image with gods/Brahmins, worships and announces: worship Dhundhi before pleasing Śiva to receive enjoyment/liberation, otherwise not; Vakratunda gives Kāśī-residence fruit. Naming the discovered Vedic root Dhundhirāja, Śiva credits him with four human aims and devotes daily service.

Yājñavalkya applies the example: worship Vighnarāja and abandon pride to become Brahmin. Viśvāmitra asks where pride resides, how to abandon it and how to worship/understand Gaṇeśa. The teacher identifies certainty that one’s own tapas must confer Brahminhood as pride. Practise sincerely but accept the deity’s grant or continued Rājarṣi status, knowing embodied dependence. Abandon competitiveness, think oneself below all Brahmins/ascetics and inwardly honor them. He reproaches Viśvāmitra’s envy: destruction of Vasiṣṭha’s100 sons as by a Rākṣasa, alternate creation for Triśaṅku and attempts on Vasiṣṭha’s life. Without reform even a thousand yugas of tapas ends in death.

Yājñavalkya recounts former Vakratunda deeds. Viśvāmitra, astonished, requests experiential teaching. Yājñavalkya promises his own past knowledge-giving story: visiting Vaikuṇṭha, he honored Nārāyaṇa and asked the essence and support of all beings, despite his intuition that all rests on Nārāyaṇa.

Nārāyaṇa says the world rests on Gaṇeśa: he gives inner buddhi and outer siddhi, is worshipped first, abides at beginning/middle/end, is Brahman-form lord of Siddhi/Buddhi while the others are guṇa-form. His Svānanda realm transcends oppositions and is inaccessible to sages/gods. Knowing him releases bonds.

Envious principles dispute who is highest and claim to create/preserve/destroy the supported world freely. Guṇādhīśa comes in Brahmin guise to end dispute and give knowledge. They wonder how he entered their Brahman paths; he says yoga made the path and asks the quarrel. Asked which principle is greatest, he proposes each leave the world in turn; the one whose departure breaks it is lord.

Earth withdraws, then water, tejas, wind, space and tanmātras, without destroying world. Five elements/tanmātras stand powerless and grieve. Five knowledge-senses, action-senses, Indra-form Brahman and illuminating deity-hosts next leave; the world remains as before and the withdrawn principles/deities lose radiance.

Anna-Brahman, prāṇa-form, mind-form, vijñāna, ānanda, nāda, bindu, so’ham, bodha, videha, asat, sat, sama-svavedya and neti-svavedya successively withdraw and world remains. Finally Svānanda-form withdraws and world dissolves.

Astonished principles praise Svānanda and ask him, their common support, to become Vināyaka, leader of all principles, and recreate the world as before. Vināyaka recreates it; Brahman-form principles reenter their own places and rejoice. Nārāyaṇa explains their Jagadīśvara titles in this framework.

Nārāyaṇa distinguishes Vināyaka as Nijānanda in saṃyoga and Nirānanda in ayoga, and yoga-form when that duality is dissolved, lord of Brahmans. Knowing him gives peace, so he urges worship. Vakratunda destroys the crooked deluding māyā by his trunk through devotion. Ga denotes mind/speech world, ṇa what exceeds it, and Gaṇeśa their lord/yoga-form; attaining him gives Brahman state. The Vedānta secret should be guarded for siddhi. Nārāyaṇa ceases, repeatedly saluting Gaṇeśa.

Yājñavalkya says he bowed to Janārdana, returned to forest, progressively mastered fivefold mental activity and attained Gaṇeśa by peace-yoga and grace. He urges Viśvāmitra’s refuge, offering Gāyatrī japa merit to Gaṇeśa and friendship to all so his name becomes meaningful. He departs honored, repeating Gaṇeśa’s name-mantra. Viśvāmitra thereafter abandons pride/envy, repeats Gāyatrī as offering to Gaṇeśa and meditates on him in tapas. Gāyatrī is called Veda-mother, Praṇava father, and Gaṇanātha’s Oṃ-shaped head/saguṇa identity explains the offering.

Soon Brahmā comes and grants Viśvāmitra Brahminhood. Vasiṣṭha with Brahmins honors and declares him Brahmin; sages rank him among seven Ṛṣis and chief Gaṇeśa devotees. He worships regularly and hymns Gaṇeśa.

Viśvāmitra hymns Gaṇeśa as guṇa lord/transcendent, knowledge-lord, elephant form, Brahman lord, first-worshipped, siddhi giver, māyā wielder/deluder, Buddhi lord, lion-mounted and also mouse-vehicle/bannered Heramba. Gaṇeśa appears lion-mounted with immeasurable solar brilliance; devotee falls tearful. He promises hymn hearers/reciters honor, desired ends, enjoyment/liberation, and invites boons. Viśvāmitra calls lineage, birth, tapas, fame and parents blessed by sight, declines māyā-objects and requests devotion and living among Gāṇapatyas to destroy māyā-delusion. Gaṇeśa says so be it, vanishes; Viśvāmitra becomes Gāṇapatya.

Mudgala says Vakratunda’s many manifestations give devotees siddhis and destroy demons; exhaustive telling is impossible. He closes the concise account to Dakṣa with benefits to faithful hearers/tellers/readers: sons/grandsons, wealth/grain, learning/lifespan, fruit of1000 Māgha months bathing at Prayāga, lifetime prescribed Kāśī residence,100,000 iṣṭāpūrta acts and complete sacrifices, and Brahman state. Sūta reports Mudgala ceased and he has repeated the account to Śaunaka, asking what he wishes next.

Sūta prescribes guarded transmission, prohibited recipients and anger warning; qualified transmission/questioning/speaking promises family uplift and destruction of Kali sins. Exact54.49 penalty clause is preserved only as unresolved evidence.
Sūta says he has told Vakratunda’s account devotionally, feels fulfilled through the assembly’s company and Gaṇeśa remembrance; following colophon ends first khaṇḍa.

Śaunaka’s assembly, satisfied yet hungry for more, asks Ekadanta’s Brahman nature, manifestations and acts. Sūta repeats Dakṣa’s request after Vakratunda’s account calmed his sacrifice-destruction grief. Dakṣa asks origin, vehicle and nature. Mudgala introduces an old Gṛtsamada–Prahlāda dialogue; Dakṣa asks first for Brahmā’s creation so Prahlāda’s context arises naturally. Mudgala agrees.

With Gaṇeśa’s boon Brahmā resolves creation, enters Janārdana through yogamāyā, hides in him and after a year emerges from his navel-lotus, becoming Viṣṇu’s son under the boon recalled here; the exact grant agency is established separately at1.13.33–37. Meditating on Heramba, his own body releases water filling ten directions; submerged and bewildered, he remembers Vakratunda for rescue. On remembrance he sees a banyan and thumb-sized sleeping Gaṇeśa on a leaf, three-eyed, four-armed, elephant-trunked, large-bellied, Śeṣa at navel, moon/crown/adornments/clothes. The child sprays Brahmā with trunk-water; delighted Brahmā begins a hymn.

Brahmā hymns leaf-sleeping Gaṇanātha/Heramba as four-armed Śeṣa-navel, elephant-faced Lambodara/Ekadanta, thumb-sized, with Siddhi/Buddhi, creation/preservation/end and māyā-delusion power, and asks rescue from creation-obstructing flood. He sees full animate/inanimate world with lords in the mouth, is carried by varied winds into the great belly, sees many cosmic eggs, and exits by a hair-pore to see the child again.

Gaṇeśa promises Brahmā’s hymn grants all aims, enjoyment/liberation and whichever thought desired to honored reciters/hearers. He diagnoses forgotten initial remembrance/worship after navel emergence as cause of obstacle, removed now by remembrance/sight. Begin every future act with remembrance/bowing and reproduce the world seen in his belly. Child disappears; Brahmā returns to lotus, performs mantra/worship and meditation; Gaṇeśa appears in heart, receives mental worship and Siddhi/Buddhi as dakṣiṇā when they arrive there, then disappears. Brahmā bows and resolves creation.

Remembering Gaṇeśa, Brahmā emits Avidyā from body, divided fivefold, red/black/white and deluding the threefold world. Tamas obscures through ignorance/body-interest; Moha produces desires/varied enjoyment-actions; Mahāmoha wrong action/sin for bodily pleasure; Tāmisra produces sickness/poverty and mental/physical affliction; Andhatāmisra produces karmic hell-torments. Avidyā remembers Gaṇeśa and pursues her purpose; Brahmā condemns her and resolves further creation.

Four sons arise from Brahmā’s body: Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra. Vidyā/jñāna is their mother-form, formless bodha/self nature. Their paths: Sanaka sahaja, Sanandana sama-yoga, Sanātana jñāna-yoga, Sanatkumāra karma-yoga. At Brahmā’s order to create remembering Gaṇeśa they create many yoga paths; displeased Brahmā tells them to stop yoga-creation and they comply.

Angry at knowledge-creation, Brahmā emits Śambhu as forehead-born son: five faces, three eyes, ten arms, half-female/male, crescent, trident, matted hair and tiger/elephant skins. Crying child asks father for place, names and task. Brahmā names Rudra for crying, Śiva as all-happiness ground, recalls boon giving son-form, assigns eight abodes earth/water/fire/wind/space/moon/sun/consecrated sacrificer and eleven names, and orders creation after Gaṇeśa meditation. Śiva creates countless immortal Rudras. Asked to create birth/death beings, he refuses and stays quiet, called Sthāṇu, celibate/upward-seeded and worshipping Gaṇeśa.

Brahmā emits Vedas with śāstras and Purāṇas from mouths and tells them to create. They propitiate Gaṇeśa by tapas, receive boons and create beings and varied rites. Brahmā rejoices, begins sacrifice and thinks of Viṣṇu to obtain him as son. Four-armed Yajña-form Janārdana emerges from sacrifice, asks father’s order and, remembering Gaṇeśa as told, creates many karma-born sacrifices granting manifold fruits like wish-trees.

Ten body-born sons appear: Marīci, Bhṛgu, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Dakṣa, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada. Ordered to create, they agree and go to forest tapas. Nārada refuses creation, choosing Gaṇanāyaka worship because world is māyā/mithyā; Brahmā insists create first, worship in old age. Nārada questions labour for delusive aims. Brahmā angrily curses Śūdra birth and woman-enjoying Gandharva life; Nārada curses Brahmā to be unworshipped for needless cursing.

Nārada propitiates Gaṇeśa by one-syllable mantra for100 divine years and requests curse removal after hymn. Gaṇeśa says he cannot falsify father’s curse because his prior boon makes Brahmā truthful. Instead he will teach Nārada as Gandharva so māyā cannot hurt him amid women; then Śūdra birth with renouncer company/knowledge, forest life and Vaiṣṇava path; after that body falls, he again becomes Brahmā’s son Nārada, worships Śambhu and learns Gaṇeśa from Nārāyaṇa to become a loved Gāṇapatya/yoga lord. Gaṇeśa disappears; narrator says Nārada undergoes curse, returns to heaven and is reborn as Śiva-devotee, then Nārāyaṇa teaches him Gāṇapatya devotion.

Dakṣa asks how Nārāyaṇa taught Nārada. Nārada sees Śaṅkara devotedly worshipping a jeweled Cintāmaṇi/Gaṇeśa image on Kailāsa, tearful and immersed in meditation, then approaches Viṣṇu at Vaikuṇṭha. He asks why Śiva, whom he regards as immutable unmanifest Brahman, worships another, and why Viṣṇu also chants Gaṇeśa’s name. Nārāyaṇa answers Gaṇeśa is yoga-peace, Siddhi/Buddhi lord in Svānanda, sole Vināyaka; the other deities gain siddhi-giving power by devotion and worship for yoga-peace.

Nārāyaṇa recounts asking Śiva the same question after his daily worship. Śiva explains Buddhi as fivefold mental activity/Prakṛti enjoying fivefold, Siddhi as manifold delusion for whose attainment mind strives, including four aims and Brahman state. Brahman-attainer has no fivefold mind, is yogin non-different from Gaṇeśa. Ga denotes saṃprajñāta, ṇa asaṃprajñāta; Gaṇeśa is their yoga-peace lord. Śiva names himself unmanifest/neti, Viṣṇu sama, and distinguishes bhava-pratyaya’s fivefold/māyā Gaṇeśa and upāya-pratyaya’s māyā-free, while direct Gaṇeśa transcends either and is attained by peace. He urges fivefold-mind abandonment to become Cintāmaṇi; Nārāyaṇa concludes Gaṇeśa grants their offices and Brahman state and is their family deity.

Nārada bows to Viṣṇu, practices forest yoga, mental Gaṇeśa meditation and mantra; after ten years Gaṇeśa appears. He bows and worships, hymns Veda-transcendent Brahman, beyond/within neither mind/speech category, Siddhi/Buddhi lord, remover of devotee obstacles and giver to nondevotees, delusion/yoga/Vināyaka/Cintāmaṇi/Ekadanta, moon-bearing, mouse-vehicle/bannered, creator/preserver/destroyer. He declares seeing Gaṇeśa removed differentiated death-delusion, attained peace-yoga/no difference, and requests supreme devotion and loving Gāṇapatya status.

Gaṇeśa grants permanent unwavering devotion, no departure from yoga, honor by yogins/all; Nārada’s hymn gives peace-yoga and bhukti/mukti to readers/hearers. He merges into Nārada’s heart, where the sage always sees him. Mudgala explicitly closes Nārada account and promises good destiny to its hearers/readers.

Śaunaka asks Sūta what five empowered deities did. Sūta follows Mudgala’s answer to Dakṣa, recounting Pārvatī’s question to Śiva: she asks Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts after the five-deity boons, preferring them to wasted speech. Śiva joyfully embraces and answers her.

Śiva praises Pārvatī’s Gaṇeśa devotion, calls devotees Brahman-formed and liberating by sight, and says seekers/deity devotees omitting Gaṇeśa fail and fall to hell; the other gods likewise consign Gaṇeśa-disregarding or reviling devotees to hell. He calls Gaṇeśa everyone’s mother/father and first-worshipped Jyeṣṭharāja, requests constant Gaṇapatya company/dwelling in every direction, and praises Gaṇeśa/devotee accounts for worldly/otherworldly happiness, devotion and Brahman attainment by speaker/questioner/listener.

Gaṇeśa’s boons create five independent unbroken worlds: Śiva/Kailāsa, Viṣṇu/Vaikuṇṭha, Sun/Sauraloka, Śakti/Śaktiloka, Brahmā/Satyaloka. Initially mutual benefactors, they grow envious and claim unique supremacy. Viṣṇu creates body-water, sleeps; algae/creeper then earth develop. For play he creates a fragrant hundred-yojana navel-lotus. Visiting Brahmā wakes/honors him but accuses deluding creation and claims all depends on his own prior creation. Viṣṇu denies deceit, claims supreme preservation enables Brahmā and has no equal.

Brahmā invites Viṣṇu to inspect his belly. Viṣṇu enters by yogamāyā, sees cosmic creation including navel-lotus Viṣṇu, finds no end, exits and acknowledges Brahmā as guru/lord, then invites him inside. Brahmā enters by yoga, sees cosmic worlds and another Brahmā, finds no end. Viṣṇu closes exits by yogamāyā; Brahmā pierces a lotus-stalk doorway by yoga and exits angrily. Viṣṇu explains play/testing, asks pardon; Brahmā reciprocally apologizes for ignorant anger and acknowledges Viṣṇu’s greatness.

Brahmā/Viṣṇu regard themselves supreme and remember Śiva, Śakti and Sun to test them. Śiva comes first and, challenged, claims universal destruction and becomes a boundless luminous liṅga extending all directions. Brahmā proposes upward/downward searches. Before descent Viṣṇu asks a boon; Brahmā offers and Viṣṇu asks him to become his son. Brahmā acknowledges being caught by the offered promise and grants future yoga-created body from Viṣṇu’s navel lotus at creation. Both search Śiva’s limits in opposite directions, find none, return weary and hymn him.

The pair hymns Śaṅkara/Rudra/time/three-eyed, Umā lord, bull-mounted first deity, asking revealed nature for fearless worship. Śiva reveals Viṣṇu left, Brahmā right and full world in liṅga. They bow and ask withdrawal; he resumes former bull-bannered form, offers desired boons pleased by hymn, and promises reciters all wishes, his favor and his world at end.

Viṣṇu directs Brahmā to request Śiva as son so he becomes Viṣṇu’s grandson. Brahmā asks; Viṣṇu repeats; Śiva grants partial manifestation as Rudra from Brahmā’s forehead. Invited to inspect their powers with knowledge-sight, Śiva finds no end of either, calls the three supreme lords.

Sun comes at remembrance, shows boundless radiant animate/inanimate form; three lose radiance and physical sight, use knowledge-sight yet find no limit. He becomes gentle, views their powers likewise without end and calls them equal. Śakti arrives, shows gross/subtle complete-world form; four take refuge finding no end. Gentle Śakti views them and declares five equal. Under Gaṇeśa’s māyā they forget prior knowledge, ask how scripture’s one lord fits five, search above/below/ten directions without result, then meditate inwardly, attain unity and peace.

Gaṇarāja shows his form in their hearts: four arms, three eyes, trunk, one tusk, fan-ears, crooked trunk/great belly, red vermilion body, Śeṣa navel, crown/ornaments, Siddhi/Buddhi, Cintāmaṇi jewel at heart. First manifested in Śaṅkara’s heart, he is asked who he is and whether the supreme Brahman lord attained through peace-yoga.

Vakratunda says he is earlier boon-giving Gaṇeśa, forgotten by his own māyā; removes Śiva’s delusion-net and restores memory, then vanishes before hymn. Śiva’s renewed meditation fails to see him; all five compare similar experiences, abandon pride and jointly hymn Vakratunda’s form, māyā and transcendence, asking appearance. He manifests before them, raises prostrate gods, promises hymn readers honor, desired ends and final sāyujya. He warns no pride: they are dependent fractional manifestations created for play, and offers secret knowledge to remove delusion and make them like him.

Five deities request knowledge. Gaṇeśa describes fourfold deha as tvam-pada and fourfold so’ham/dehī as tat-pada; union as asi-pada with self-arising distinction, Sāṃkhya as self-bliss/other-arising, Svānanda beyond both as nondifference/union. He maps five forms: Śakti as asat; Sun as immortal/self support; Viṣṇu as Śakti/Sun delight; Śiva as fourth neti beyond three; their nondifference Svānanda. Brahmā is māyā reflection of five, creating all as Prapitāmaha. Terms retain source’s doctrinal vocabulary, not imported school equivalences.

Gaṇeśa contrasts ayoga beyond Svānanda with no entry/vision and self-experienced vision in Svānanda; yoga beyond saṃyoga/ayoga gives complete peace through mental-activity restraint. Five mental grounds are kṣipta,mūḍha,vikṣipta,ekāgra,nirodhaka, with Cintāmaṇi there; restraining them attains him as peace in heart. Buddhi is mind, Siddhi delusion, their lord plays through Brahman distinctions. Give up worry/pride in Gaṇeśa-identity samādhi to become his form without delusion. He ceases, gods abandon difference and instantly gain peace. Śiva calls the teaching21 verses; faithful reading/hearing gives Brahman likeness, worldly enjoyment then yoga, and others’ sins vanish by sight of such a person.

Gods ask how guṇa-forms are Brahman. Gaṇeśa says they are Brahman in own states, guṇa in distinction, created for play.
